title: Global Procurement Policy — Approval Thresholds and Delegation of Authority
text:
Purpose and Scope

This Policy defines the approval authority required before Vantera Group N.V. or any of its subsidiaries commits expenditure to a third party. It applies to all indirect and direct spend, capital expenditure, contingent labour, and intercompany purchases routed through the Ariba Buying and SAP S/4HANA landscape. It applies to every employee, contractor, and agency worker who raises a purchase requisition, approves spend, or signs a contract on behalf of a Vantera entity. Local procedures may impose stricter controls than this Policy, but may never relax them.

Core Principle

No supplier may begin work, ship goods, or incur cost on behalf of Vantera before an approved purchase order exists in SAP S/4HANA. Approval is granted against the total committed value of the commitment, not against the value of an individual invoice, an individual release, or the amount falling into the current fiscal year. For a multi-year agreement, total committed value means the aggregate charge over the full contractual term including all committed renewals, licence uplifts, indexation at the contractually agreed cap, and any minimum volume commitment. Where the value cannot be determined precisely, the requester must use a documented good-faith estimate at the upper end of the expected range, and re-approve if the actual value exceeds the approved band.

Approval Bands

The following approval bands apply to the total committed value expressed in EUR. Amounts in other currencies are converted at the monthly Group corporate rate published by Treasury on the first working day of each month.

Band 1 (below €5,000): approval by the Budget Owner for the cost centre being charged.
Band 2 (€5,000 up to and including €50,000): approval by the responsible Category Manager in addition to the Budget Owner.
Band 3 (above €50,000 up to and including €250,000): approval by the VP Procurement, supported by a documented Finance review of budget availability and business case.
Band 4 (above €250,000 up to and including €1,000,000): approval by the Chief Procurement Officer and the Chief Financial Officer.
Band 5 (above €1,000,000 up to and including €5,000,000): approval by the Executive Committee, minuted in the Executive Committee record.
Band 6 (above €5,000,000): approval by the Board Investment Committee following Executive Committee endorsement.

Approvals are cumulative and not alternative. A Band 4 commitment requires the Budget Owner, the Category Manager, the VP Procurement, the CPO, and the CFO to have approved, in that sequence, before a purchase order is released to the supplier.

Segregation of Duties

The person who raises a requisition may not approve it, regardless of their delegated authority. The person who approves a purchase order may not perform goods receipt for that order, and may not release the corresponding payment run. Requisitions may not be split into smaller commitments to avoid a higher approval band. Splitting is defined as two or more requisitions raised within a rolling 90-day period, for the same supplier and the same scope of work, whose combined value would have required a higher band. Detected splitting is reported to Internal Audit as a control breach and is reported quarterly to the Audit Committee.

Delegation During Absence

An approver may delegate their authority temporarily using the formal delegation function in SAP S/4HANA, and only to an employee at the same grade or above. Delegation by email, verbal instruction, or shared credentials is prohibited. A delegation may not exceed 30 consecutive calendar days without renewal, and the delegating approver remains accountable for decisions taken under their authority.

Emergency Purchases

Where a genuine business continuity risk exists, for example a production line stoppage, a food safety incident, or a security incident, work may begin before a purchase order is issued with verbal approval from an approver holding the appropriate band authority. The requester must document the emergency reason, the estimated spend, the supplier name, and the name of the approving manager within 2 business days, and a retrospective purchase order must be raised within 5 business days. Emergency purchases are reported monthly to the VP Procurement, and any cost centre exceeding six emergency purchases in a rolling 12-month period is subject to a process review.

Contract Signature Authority

Approval of spend and signature of a contract are separate acts. A purchase order approval does not confer authority to sign a contract, a statement of work, an order form, a licence agreement, or a non-disclosure agreement. Contract signature authority is held under the Group Signature Authority Schedule, and any agreement containing non-standard liability, indemnity, or intellectual property terms requires Legal review before signature regardless of value.

Non-Compliance

Commitments made outside this Policy are treated as unauthorised commitments. The requesting manager is responsible for regularising the commitment through a retrospective approval, which must be approved one band above the band that would ordinarily have applied. Repeated unauthorised commitments are addressed through the disciplinary process and are a mandatory reporting item in the annual Sarbanes-Oxley control certification.

Related Documents

This Policy should be read together with the Competitive Sourcing and Bidding Policy, the Supplier Payment Terms and Working Capital Policy, the standard operating procedure for requisition to purchase order intake, and the Group Signature Authority Schedule.

Document Control

title: Supplier Onboarding and Third-Party Due Diligence Policy
text:
Purpose and Scope

This Policy sets the minimum due diligence that must be completed before a third party is created in the supplier master and becomes eligible to receive a purchase order or a payment from any Vantera entity. It covers suppliers of goods and services, agencies, intermediaries, distributors, consultants, and one-time payees. It does not cover employees, tax authorities, or statutory bodies, which are governed by separate Finance procedures.

Mandatory Onboarding Checks

No supplier record may be activated in SAP MDG-S until all of the following have been completed and evidenced in the Ariba Supplier Information Management workflow. Know Your Supplier identity verification confirms the legal entity, the registered address, the company registration number, and the ultimate beneficial ownership where a shareholder holds 25% or more. Sanctions and watchlist screening is performed against the Dow Jones Risk and Compliance dataset covering EU, UN, OFAC, and UK HMT lists, and must return a clear result or a documented false-positive disposition approved by Compliance. Tax validation confirms the VAT identification number through the VIES service for EU suppliers, or the equivalent national registry elsewhere, and captures a valid tax residency certificate where withholding tax relief is claimed. Bank account verification confirms that the account belongs to the legal entity being onboarded, through an independent callback to a telephone number obtained from the supplier's registered public record, never from the invoice, the supplier's email signature, or the onboarding form itself. Financial health screening retrieves a Dun and Bradstreet failure score, and any supplier scoring in the highest risk quartile is escalated to the Supplier Risk Office before activation.

Legal Name Accuracy

The supplier name recorded in the supplier master must match the name on the certificate of incorporation or equivalent registration document exactly, including legal form suffixes such as S.L., S.L.U., S.A., GmbH, Ltd., Inc., B.V., N.V., AG, and Sp. z o.o. Trading names, abbreviations, and group brand names must be recorded in the alias field rather than the legal name field. This matters operationally as well as legally. Payment rejection, duplicate supplier records, failed sanctions screening, and failed contract matching are all commonly traced to a legal name that was entered as a convenient short form.

Risk Classification

Every supplier is classified at onboarding and re-classified at each contract renewal. Low risk covers standard goods and services below €100,000 annual spend with no access to personal data, no work on Vantera premises, and no operation in a high-risk jurisdiction. Medium risk covers annual spend between €100,000 and €500,000, or any supplier with access to Vantera systems or premises. High risk covers annual spend above €500,000, any supplier processing personal data or confidential business data, any supplier acting as an intermediary before a public official, any supplier in a country scoring below 45 on the Transparency International Corruption Perceptions Index, and any supplier in a category with recognised human rights exposure such as facilities services, agricultural raw materials, or contingent labour.

Enhanced Due Diligence

High-risk suppliers require Enhanced Due Diligence before activation and formal approval from Legal. Enhanced Due Diligence adds adverse media screening covering the previous five years, verification of ultimate beneficial ownership through an independent registry extract rather than self-declaration, a completed anti-bribery and corruption questionnaire signed by an officer of the supplier, and a review of any politically exposed person connection. Where a high-risk supplier will process personal data, the information security and data protection assessment must also be completed before go-live. Enhanced Due Diligence evidence is retained for seven years from the end of the commercial relationship.

Service Levels

Standard onboarding is completed within 10 business days from receipt of a complete supplier submission. Expedited onboarding is completed within 3 business days and requires VP Procurement approval of the business reason. The clock stops whenever the file is returned to the supplier for missing information, and the Supplier Risk Office reports monthly on cycle time, first-time-right rate, and the volume of expedited requests.

Ongoing Monitoring

Sanctions screening is re-run automatically every night against the full active supplier master, and any new hit blocks payment until dispositioned. Ultimate beneficial ownership is refreshed every 24 months for high-risk suppliers. A supplier that has received no purchase order for 24 consecutive months is set to inactive, and reactivation requires the full onboarding check set to be repeated rather than merely unblocked.

Prohibited Practices

A requester may not create a supplier record on behalf of a supplier, may not accept bank details communicated by email without callback verification, and may not use a one-time payee record to bypass onboarding for a recurring supplier relationship. Onboarding a supplier in order to place a purchase order with an entity that has already been rejected under this Policy, under a different legal name, is a serious control breach and is reported to Internal Audit.

Document Control

title: Information Security and Data Protection Requirements for Technology Suppliers
section_headings: Restrictions on Model Training and Secondary Use
text:
Purpose and Scope

This Policy defines the security and data protection evidence that a technology supplier must provide before it may host, process, transmit, or access Vantera data. It applies to software as a service, infrastructure and platform services, managed service providers, analytics and marketing platforms, artificial intelligence services, and any supplier granted remote access to a Vantera system. It applies at initial sourcing, at renewal, and whenever the scope of data processing materially changes.

Data Classification Drives the Requirement

The controls required depend on the classification of the data the supplier will handle. Class A covers personal data of employees, consumers, or business contacts, and any special category data. Class B covers confidential commercial data including pricing, cost models, supplier terms, recipes, and unreleased commercial plans. Class C covers internal data with limited sensitivity. Class D covers public data. A supplier handling Class A or Class B data is a Tier-1 data supplier for the purposes of this Policy, regardless of contract value.

Minimum Certification Evidence

Any supplier handling Vantera data must provide a current ISO 27001 certificate or a SOC 2 Type II report. The certificate scope statement must cover the specific service and hosting environment being purchased, not merely the supplier's corporate headquarters, and a SOC 2 Type II report must cover an observation period of at least six months ending no more than twelve months before the assessment date. Tier-1 data suppliers must provide both an ISO 27001 certificate and a SOC 2 Type II report, together with the executive summary of an independent penetration test performed within the previous 12 months, and a remediation status for any critical or high finding.

Contractual Requirements

Every contract with a supplier in scope must include a breach notification obligation requiring the supplier to notify Vantera without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of becoming aware of a personal data breach or a security incident affecting Vantera data. Individual contracts may impose a shorter notification window, and where they do, the shorter window prevails. Contracts must include data processing terms, a right to conduct an annual security review or to receive the results of an equivalent independent assessment, an obligation to maintain the certifications relied upon at selection, a requirement to encrypt Vantera data in transit using TLS 1.2 or above and at rest using AES-256 or an equivalent standard, and an obligation to return or securely delete Vantera data on termination within a defined period.

Data Protection Agreements

A supplier that processes personal data on behalf of a Vantera entity must sign a data processing agreement on the Vantera template before go-live, without exception and regardless of contract value. The data processing agreement must record the categories of data subject, the categories of personal data, the purpose and duration of processing, the technical and organisational measures applied, and the approved list of sub-processors. Any transfer of personal data outside the European Economic Area requires an adequacy decision or Standard Contractual Clauses supported by a documented transfer impact assessment. Sub-processor changes must be notified in advance, with a defined objection period for Vantera.

Restrictions on Model Training and Secondary Use

Vantera data may not be used to train, fine-tune, evaluate, or improve any machine learning or artificial intelligence model without prior written approval from the Chief Data Officer and the Data Protection Officer. This restriction applies to aggregated and pseudonymised derivatives of Vantera data as well as to raw data, and it must be reflected as an express contractual prohibition rather than a supplier policy statement. Suppliers offering artificial intelligence features must confirm in writing whether prompts, uploaded documents, and outputs are retained, and for how long.

Availability and Resilience

Standard software as a service agreements must include a monthly availability commitment of at least 99.5%, measured excluding agreed maintenance windows, with a defined service credit regime. Services supporting a business-critical process require at least 99.9% availability, a documented recovery time objective and recovery point objective, and evidence that the supplier tests its business continuity and disaster recovery plan at least annually.

Assessment Process and Timing

The security assessment is initiated at the shortlist stage of a sourcing event, not after award. A supplier that cannot evidence the required controls may be awarded only where a time-bound remediation plan is agreed, the residual risk is formally accepted by the accountable business owner and the Chief Information Security Officer, and the acceptance is recorded in the risk register with a review date. Risk acceptance may not exceed 12 months and may not be renewed more than once.

Renewal and Continuous Assurance

Certification evidence is refreshed annually. A lapsed certificate is treated as a control failure and triggers a review of whether the service may continue. Tier-1 data suppliers are re-assessed in full every 24 months, and after any reported breach affecting Vantera data.

Document Control

title: Competitive Sourcing and Bidding Policy
text:
Purpose and Scope

This Policy establishes when competition is required before an award, what form that competition must take, and how competitive events must be documented so that an award can be defended to Internal Audit, to the external auditor, and to unsuccessful bidders. It applies to all new awards, to renewals, and to material scope extensions of existing agreements.

Competition Requirements by Value

Competition requirements are based on the total committed value of the award as defined in the Global Procurement Policy.

Below €25,000: no formal competition required, although the buyer should evidence that pricing is reasonable, for example through a catalogue price, a published rate, or a prior comparable purchase.
€25,000 up to €250,000: at least three qualified bids must be obtained and compared on a like-for-like basis.
Above €250,000: a formal request for proposal must be run through Ariba Sourcing, with a written scope of work, a published evaluation model, and a documented award recommendation.
Above €1,000,000: a formal request for proposal is required together with a category strategy approved by the Category Council before the event is launched.

A qualified bid means a bid from a supplier that is capable of performing the scope, has passed onboarding due diligence or is capable of passing it before award, and has responded to the same scope and commercial terms as the other bidders. Three quotations obtained from suppliers who were never realistically capable of winning do not constitute three qualified bids, and this practice is treated as a control breach rather than a technicality.

Evaluation Integrity

The evaluation model, including criteria and weightings, must be defined and approved before bids are opened. Weightings may not be changed after bid opening. Price may not exceed 60% of the total evaluation weighting for any category, and for services categories where quality of delivery drives value, price should normally sit between 30% and 50%. Evaluation must be performed by a panel of at least three people, of whom at least one is from the requesting business function and at least one is from Procurement. Individual scores and the consensus rationale are recorded in Ariba Sourcing and retained for seven years.

Confidentiality and Fair Dealing

Bidder pricing may not be disclosed to another bidder, in aggregate or in detail. Bid clarification questions of general relevance and their answers are shared with all bidders simultaneously. A best and final offer round may be run once, must be offered to all shortlisted bidders on the same terms, and may not be used to reveal a competitor's price. Reverse auctions require prior approval from the VP Procurement and are prohibited for categories where quality, safety, or human rights risk is a material differentiator.

Permitted Exceptions to Competition

Competition may be waived only in the following circumstances, and only with a documented and approved sourcing exception. Sole source applies where only one supplier can supply the requirement, for example because of a patent, a proprietary interface, a regulatory approval, or an exclusive distribution right, and the sole-source position must be evidenced rather than asserted. Emergency continuity applies where a delay would create a safety, regulatory, or production continuity risk. Regulated utilities and statutory charges are exempt because pricing is set externally. Renewal with benchmark evidence permits an incumbent renewal without competition where documented market benchmark data, obtained within the previous 12 months, demonstrates that current pricing remains competitive. Intercompany and group-mandated arrangements are exempt where the arrangement itself was competitively sourced at group level.

Exception Governance

A sourcing exception requires a written business justification, the name and role of the approver, and an audit trail entry in Ariba Sourcing. The approval authority for an exception is one band above the approval authority for the underlying spend. An exception is valid for a maximum of 12 months, and no requirement may be renewed under a sourcing exception more than twice consecutively without a competitive event or a Category Council decision. The Procurement Governance team reports the exception rate by category and by business unit quarterly, and a business unit whose exception rate exceeds 15% of addressable spend is subject to a formal remediation plan.

Award and Communication

The award recommendation records the evaluation outcome, the negotiated savings against the baseline, the risk assessment result, and the recommended supplier. Unsuccessful bidders are informed within 10 business days of award and are offered feedback on the strengths and weaknesses of their proposal, without disclosing competitor information. No contract may be signed and no purchase order released until the award approval is complete under the Global Procurement Policy.

Document Control

title: Anti-Bribery, Gifts, Hospitality and Conflict of Interest Policy — Procurement Application
text:
Purpose and Scope

This Policy sets out how anti-bribery and corruption obligations apply to procurement activity across the Vantera Group. It reflects the UK Bribery Act 2010, the United States Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, the Dutch Criminal Code, and equivalent legislation in the countries where Vantera operates. It applies to all employees involved in supplier selection, negotiation, contract award, performance management, and payment approval, and it applies equally to third parties acting on Vantera's behalf.

Prohibited Conduct

Offering, promising, giving, requesting, agreeing to receive, or accepting any financial or other advantage intended to induce or reward improper performance is prohibited without exception. This applies whether the advantage is offered directly or through an intermediary such as an agent, distributor, consultant, customs broker, or joint venture partner. Facilitation payments, being small unofficial payments made to secure or expedite a routine governmental action, are prohibited in all jurisdictions, including where local practice tolerates them. The only exception is a payment made under genuine and imminent threat to personal safety, which must be reported to Group Compliance within 24 hours of the individual reaching safety.

Gifts and Hospitality Thresholds

Gifts and hospitality are permitted only where they are proportionate, infrequent, transparent, offered without expectation of reciprocity, and never given or received in cash or cash equivalent such as gift cards, vouchers, or cryptocurrency.

Below €100 per item: acceptable without prior approval, provided it is not offered during a live sourcing event.
€100 up to €250 per item: permitted only with prior approval from the line manager, and must be recorded in the Gifts and Hospitality Register within 5 business days.
Above €250 per item: prohibited, and any such gift received must be declined, or where declining would cause offence, accepted on behalf of Vantera, surrendered, and recorded.

Travel and accommodation paid for by a supplier is prohibited. Where a supplier hosts a site visit, a factory audit, or a user conference that Vantera genuinely needs to attend, Vantera pays its own travel and accommodation costs.

The Live Sourcing Event Rule

From the moment a sourcing event is announced to the market until the award decision is communicated to all bidders, no member of the evaluation panel may accept any gift or hospitality of any value from any participating bidder, including meals, event tickets, and site-visit catering beyond ordinary working refreshments. This rule is absolute because the appearance of influence during a live competition is as damaging as influence itself.

Conflicts of Interest

A conflict of interest exists where a personal, financial, or family interest could reasonably be seen to influence a procurement decision. Examples include a close family member employed by or owning a stake in a bidder, a personal financial interest in a bidder, a prospective employment discussion with a bidder, a personal relationship with a bidder's account team, and any outside business activity that competes or transacts with Vantera. Every member of an evaluation panel must complete a conflict of interest declaration before receiving access to bid documents, and must update it immediately if circumstances change. A declared conflict does not automatically disqualify an individual, but the mitigation, which may be recusal from scoring, recusal from the category entirely, or additional oversight, is decided by Procurement Governance and recorded with the event.

Third-Party Risk

Third parties that interact with public officials on Vantera's behalf, including customs brokers, licensing agents, and government relations consultants, are subject to Enhanced Due Diligence before engagement and to re-screening every 24 months. Contracts with such third parties must include anti-bribery representations, audit rights over the relevant books and records, an obligation to cooperate with investigations, and a right of immediate termination for breach. Commission arrangements based on a percentage of contract value in high-risk jurisdictions require Group Compliance approval, and success fees payable on the grant of a licence, permit, or approval by a public body are prohibited.

Red Flags

Buyers must escalate to Group Compliance where they encounter a supplier that requests payment to a third country or to an account in a name different from the contracting entity, a supplier that resists anti-bribery contractual terms or audit rights, an intermediary that cannot explain the service it provides, an unusually high commission relative to the market, a request for an unusual discount structure combined with a request for a personal benefit, or pressure to bypass competitive sourcing in favour of a specific named supplier without a documented reason.

Reporting and Protection

Concerns are reported to the line manager, to Group Compliance, or anonymously through the Speak Up line, which is available in all operating languages and operated by an independent provider. Vantera prohibits retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith, including where the concern is ultimately not substantiated.

Consequences

Breach of this Policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including dismissal, termination of supplier contracts, and referral to law enforcement. Individuals may be personally criminally liable, and under the UK Bribery Act a failure by Vantera to prevent bribery by an associated person is itself a corporate offence, which is why adequate procedures, including the due diligence and record-keeping required by this Policy, must be followed and evidenced.

Document Control

Policy owner: Group Compliance. Version 5.1 effective 2026-01-05. Next review 2027-01-05. Mandatory annual training applies to all procurement staff and to budget owners above Band 2 authority.

title: Responsible Sourcing, Human Rights and Environmental Requirements Policy
text:
Purpose and Scope

This Policy defines the environmental, social, and human rights requirements that apply to Vantera's supply base, and the due diligence Vantera performs to meet its obligations under the German Supply Chain Due Diligence Act, the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, the EU Deforestation Regulation, the UK Modern Slavery Act 2015, and the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive as transposed. It applies to all direct and indirect suppliers, and it extends to sub-suppliers where Vantera has substantiated knowledge of a risk.

The Supplier Code of Conduct

Every supplier must accept the Vantera Supplier Code of Conduct, either by signature during onboarding or by incorporation into the contract by reference. Where a supplier proposes its own equivalent code, Sustainable Procurement performs a gap assessment, and the supplier's code may be accepted only where it is at least as protective on forced labour, child labour, freedom of association, working hours, wages, health and safety, and environmental compliance. Acceptance of the Code is a precondition of award and is not negotiable for suppliers in high-risk categories.

Assessment Requirements

Suppliers with annual spend above €250,000 must complete an EcoVadis assessment and achieve a minimum overall score of 45 out of 100. Tier 1 strategic suppliers must reach EcoVadis Silver, being a score of 59 or above, by 2027-01-01. A supplier scoring below 45 is not automatically disqualified, but may be awarded only against a corrective action plan with defined milestones, and is re-assessed within 12 months. A supplier that fails to improve across two consecutive assessments is escalated to the Category Council for a decision on continued engagement.

High-Risk Categories

The following categories are treated as inherently high risk for human rights due diligence regardless of spend, and require an on-site social audit before award and every 24 months thereafter: facilities services and cleaning, security services, contingent and agency labour, logistics and warehousing where agency labour is used, agricultural raw materials, packaging with a recycled fibre supply chain, and any category with production in a country classified as high risk in the Vantera country risk index. Audits follow the SMETA four-pillar methodology or an accepted equivalent, and are performed by an independent audit body, never by the supplier itself.

Salient Human Rights Issues

Vantera's salient issues are forced labour and debt bondage in agency labour supply chains, excessive working hours in facilities and logistics, wage underpayment and unlawful deductions, unsafe working conditions in warehousing and manufacturing, discrimination and harassment, and restrictions on freedom of association. Contracts in high-risk categories must include a prohibition on recruitment fees charged to workers, the requirement that workers retain possession of their identity documents, a living wage commitment where a credible local benchmark exists, and a right for Vantera to conduct unannounced audits.

Grievance Mechanism

Vantera operates a supply chain grievance mechanism accessible to workers employed by suppliers, available in the principal languages of the supply base, with an option for anonymous reporting. Suppliers must inform their workers of the mechanism and must not retaliate against a worker who uses it. Substantiated grievances are remediated jointly with the supplier, and remediation is tracked to closure by the Supplier Risk Office. A supplier that obstructs the grievance process, retaliates against a complainant, or conceals findings from an audit is subject to immediate escalation and possible termination.

Environmental Requirements

Suppliers must comply with applicable environmental law as a minimum. The top 100 suppliers by emissions relevance must provide primary Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions data annually, together with the methodology used, to support Vantera's Scope 3 category 1 reporting. Suppliers of soy, palm oil, cocoa, coffee, cattle products, rubber, and wood must provide geolocation data for the plots of production and evidence of deforestation-free status in line with the EU Deforestation Regulation, and must transmit the associated due diligence statement reference before shipment into the European Union.

Packaging and Circularity

Packaging suppliers must support Vantera's commitment that all packaging is reusable, recyclable, or compostable, must provide material composition data by component, and must disclose recycled content percentages with supporting evidence. Substrate changes that affect recyclability require written approval from Vantera Packaging Development before implementation.

Contractual Integration and Termination

Responsible sourcing obligations must be included in every contract above €100,000, and must include audit rights, corrective action obligations, and a right to terminate for a serious and unremedied breach. Vantera's approach is to remediate rather than to withdraw, because abrupt withdrawal frequently harms the workers the Policy exists to protect. Termination is nonetheless applied where a supplier is unwilling to remediate, where forced or child labour is confirmed and not immediately addressed, or where the supplier conceals material information.

Reporting

Sustainable Procurement reports quarterly on assessment coverage, average EcoVadis score by category, audit findings by severity, open corrective actions, and grievance case status. These metrics feed the annual sustainability statement and the LkSG report filed by Vantera Deutschland GmbH.

Document Control

title: Supplier Payment Terms and Working Capital Policy
section_headings: Mandatory Exceptions to the Standard Term
Early Payment and Supply Chain Finance
text:
Purpose and Scope

This Policy defines standard payment terms for supplier contracts, the limited circumstances in which non-standard terms may be agreed, and the controls that govern payment execution. It applies to all Vantera entities and to all supplier categories, and it is written to balance working capital objectives against legal obligations and supply base health.

Standard Payment Terms

The Vantera standard payment term is Net 60 days from the date of receipt of a valid invoice. The clock starts on receipt of a valid invoice, not on the invoice date and not on the date the supplier claims to have sent it. An invoice is valid only where it quotes a valid purchase order number, matches the purchase order and the goods receipt, quotes the correct legal entity and VAT registration, and is submitted through the Ariba Network or the designated invoicing channel for the entity.

Mandatory Exceptions to the Standard Term

Certain suppliers must be paid on shorter terms. Suppliers qualifying as small or medium-sized enterprises, defined as annual turnover below €10,000,000, are paid Net 30 as a matter of policy, and buyers must not negotiate longer terms with an SME supplier in exchange for volume. Where national law caps commercial payment terms, the legal cap prevails; in Spain the statutory maximum for commercial transactions is 60 days and no contractual extension is permitted, and in France the standard legal maximum is 60 days from invoice date or 45 days end of month. Public sector counterparties, regulated utilities, statutory bodies, and insurance premiums follow the terms set by the counterparty or by law.

Non-Standard Terms

A payment term longer than Net 60 requires approval from the VP Procurement and Group Treasury, and may not be applied to an SME supplier. A payment term shorter than Net 30 requires Group Treasury approval, because it consumes working capital, and is normally granted only where the supplier offers a corresponding commercial benefit, where it is required by law, or where it is necessary to secure continuity of a critical supply. Prepayment and deposits require VP Procurement approval, must be justified by the commercial context such as bespoke tooling or a capital equipment build, must be no larger than necessary, and above €100,000 must be secured by an advance payment guarantee from an investment-grade bank.

Early Payment and Supply Chain Finance

Vantera offers two mechanisms that allow a supplier to be paid earlier than the contractual term. A static early payment discount of 2% for payment within 10 days is available on request and is applied at invoice level. The supply chain finance programme allows an approved supplier to receive payment from a funding bank shortly after invoice approval, at a discount rate based on Vantera's credit rating rather than the supplier's, while Vantera pays the bank on the original due date. Participation is voluntary for the supplier, participation or non-participation may not be used as leverage in a negotiation, and terms may not be extended as a condition of offering supply chain finance.

No Purchase Order, No Payment

Accounts Payable will not process an invoice that does not reference a valid purchase order. The limited exempt categories are utilities, property rent and service charges, taxes and statutory fees, payroll and pension payments, insurance premiums, legal settlements, intercompany recharges, and customs duties. Any other invoice received without a purchase order is returned to the supplier with a copy to the requesting manager, and the requesting manager is responsible for raising a retrospective purchase order under the exception process. Persistent no-purchase-order invoicing by a business unit is reported to the VP Procurement monthly.

Payment Execution Controls

Payment runs are executed centrally, twice weekly for euro-denominated payments and weekly for other currencies. Any change to supplier bank details places a 24-hour hold on payments to that supplier and requires independent verification before release. Manual and urgent payments outside the scheduled run require dual approval, one of whom must be from Treasury, and are reported monthly with the business reason. Duplicate payment detection runs before each payment run against supplier, amount, invoice number, and date proximity.

Disputes and Withholding

Where an invoice is disputed, the undisputed portion is paid on the original due date and only the disputed portion is withheld. Withholding an entire invoice because of a partial dispute is not permitted, because it damages supplier relationships and frequently causes escalations that cost more to resolve than the disputed amount. The buyer must record the dispute reason in the system within 5 business days of the dispute being raised.

Measurement

Procure-to-Pay reports monthly on days payable outstanding, on-time payment rate against contractual terms, the proportion of spend under standard terms, first-time-right invoice rate, and the volume and ageing of blocked invoices. On-time payment rate is a supplier-facing commitment and is reviewed in every Tier 1 quarterly business review.

Document Control

Policy owner: Group Treasury jointly with Procure-to-Pay. Version 3.3 effective 2026-01-01. Next review 2027-01-01.

title: Contract Standards Policy — Liability, Insurance, Term and Termination
text:
Purpose and Scope

This Policy defines the contractual positions Vantera treats as standard, the positions that require Legal review, and the positions that may not be accepted without escalation. It applies to master services agreements, supply agreements, framework agreements, statements of work, order forms, licence agreements, and any supplier terms incorporated by reference.

Order of Precedence

Every agreement must state an order of precedence. The Vantera standard order places the master agreement above any statement of work, and any statement of work above supplier standard terms, purchase order terms, and any online or click-through terms. Supplier standard terms incorporated by a hyperlink are accepted only where the version is fixed by reference to a date or a version number, because a hyperlink to terms the supplier can unilaterally change is not an agreed contractual position.

Limitation of Liability

The standard Vantera position caps each party's aggregate liability at 150% of the charges paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. Liability may not be capped, and must be expressly excluded from the cap, for breach of confidentiality, breach of data protection obligations, infringement of intellectual property rights, death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful misconduct, and a party's indemnity obligations. A liability cap below 100% of annual charges, a cap expressed as a fixed sum unrelated to contract value, or a mutual exclusion of all indirect losses that captures loss of data or wasted expenditure, each require Legal approval. Exclusion of the supplier's liability for loss of profit is acceptable only where the exclusion is mutual.

Indemnities

The supplier must indemnify Vantera against third-party claims arising from infringement of intellectual property rights, from the supplier's breach of data protection obligations, from personal injury or property damage caused by the supplier's negligence, and from the supplier's breach of applicable law including anti-bribery and employment law. Where the supplier provides personnel who work on Vantera premises or under Vantera direction, the contract must also address employment status and co-employment risk.

Insurance Minimums

Suppliers must maintain, and evidence annually through a broker's certificate, at least the following cover. General third-party liability of €5,000,000 per occurrence. Professional indemnity of €2,000,000 per claim for consultancy, design, engineering, and advisory services. Cyber liability of €5,000,000 for Tier-1 data suppliers as defined in the information security policy. Product liability of €10,000,000 for suppliers of food-contact materials, ingredients, and finished goods. Employer's liability at the statutory minimum, or £5,000,000 in the United Kingdom. Motor and goods-in-transit cover appropriate to the service for logistics suppliers.

Intellectual Property

Vantera owns all intellectual property in deliverables specifically created for Vantera under a statement of work, including designs, artwork, formulations, and bespoke software, and the contract must assign those rights with full title guarantee. Where a supplier uses its pre-existing intellectual property in a deliverable, it retains ownership of that background intellectual property but must grant Vantera a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use it to the extent necessary to exploit the deliverable. Supplier claims to ownership of data generated from Vantera's use of a service, or of insights derived from Vantera data, must be rejected.

Term, Renewal and Termination

The standard initial term is three years for strategic categories and one to two years for competitive commodity categories. Automatic renewal is permitted only where Vantera holds a right to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice or less, and evergreen terms with no exit right are not accepted. Vantera requires a right to terminate for convenience on not more than 90 days' notice, a right to terminate for material breach not remedied within 30 days of written notice, and a right to terminate immediately on insolvency, change of control to a competitor, or a serious compliance breach. Termination for convenience compensation is limited to committed costs that the supplier cannot reasonably mitigate, evidenced by documentation.

Exit and Transition Assistance

Contracts for services that would be disruptive to replace must include exit assistance obligations of at least 90 days at agreed rates, an obligation to return Vantera data in a documented, non-proprietary format, an obligation to delete remaining copies within a defined period, and a prohibition on withholding data or services because of a commercial dispute.

Audit and Records

Vantera requires the right to audit the supplier's compliance with the contract, including open-book cost data where a cost-plus or indexation mechanism applies, on 10 business days' notice, no more than once in any 12-month period unless a material breach is suspected. The supplier must retain relevant records for seven years.

Governing Law and Escalation

Agreements with EU Vantera entities are governed by Dutch law with exclusive jurisdiction in Amsterdam, and agreements with Vantera UK Ltd. are governed by the law of England and Wales. Disputes follow a contractual escalation ladder before litigation, and arbitration is used only where cross-border enforcement makes it clearly preferable.

Document Control

Policy owner: Legal — Commercial Contracts. Version 2.0 effective 2026-05-01. Next review 2027-05-01. Deviations from the positions in this Policy must be recorded in the contract approval record in Ariba Contracts.

title: Standard Operating Procedure — Three-Bid Requirement and Sourcing Exception Handling
section_headings: What Counts as a Qualified Bid
Exception Grounds and the Evidence Required
text:
Purpose

This procedure explains how a buyer obtains and documents three qualified bids, and how a sourcing exception is requested, approved, and recorded when competition is not possible. It operationalises the Competitive Sourcing and Bidding Policy and is the document Internal Audit uses when testing award controls.

When Three Bids Are Required

Three qualified bids are required for any award with a total committed value above €25,000 and up to €250,000. Above €250,000 a formal request for proposal replaces the three-bid process. Below €25,000 competition is not mandatory, although price reasonableness must still be evidenced. The threshold is assessed against the total committed value over the full term, so a two-year service at €15,000 per year is a €30,000 commitment and requires three bids.

Running a Three-Bid Comparison

The buyer prepares a written requirement covering scope, volumes, service levels, delivery locations, and the commercial terms expected, and issues the same document to all invited suppliers on the same day with the same response deadline. The response deadline must allow at least 10 business days for a standard requirement and at least 15 business days where the supplier must visit a site or prepare a design. Bids are received through Ariba Sourcing rather than by email, so that the receipt timestamp and the sealed-bid control are preserved. Bids are compared on a like-for-like basis using a total cost of ownership view that includes unit price, freight and duties on the agreed Incoterm, implementation and onboarding costs, exit costs, payment terms expressed as a working capital value, and any assumptions the supplier has attached to its price.

What Counts as a Qualified Bid

A bid is qualified where the supplier is capable of performing the scope at the required volume, has passed onboarding due diligence or can pass it before award, has responded to the same scope as the other bidders, and has submitted a price that is intended as a genuine offer. A courtesy quotation from a supplier known to be uncompetitive, a quotation for a materially different scope, and a quotation from a supplier the buyer knows cannot meet the required volumes are not qualified bids. Where fewer than three qualified bids are received despite a genuine market approach, the buyer documents which suppliers were invited, when, and what response each gave, and this record supports an exception on the ground of limited market response.

Requesting a Sourcing Exception

An exception is requested in Ariba Sourcing using the sourcing exception form before the award, never afterwards. The form requires the requirement description and total committed value, the exception ground relied upon, the evidence supporting that ground, the alternatives considered and why they were rejected, the proposed supplier and the basis on which the price is considered reasonable, and the duration of the exception requested. Retrospective exceptions are recorded separately as control breaches, and the buyer must state why the exception was not requested in advance.

Exception Grounds and the Evidence Required

Sole source requires evidence that only one supplier can meet the requirement, such as a patent reference, a proprietary interface or protocol, an exclusive distribution letter from the manufacturer, a regulatory approval held only by that supplier, or a validated qualification that a competitor would take longer to obtain than the business can wait. An internal preference for an incumbent is not a sole-source ground.
Emergency continuity requires a description of the operational, safety, or regulatory consequence of delay, and the name of the manager who confirmed it.
Regulated utilities and statutory charges require only identification of the tariff or statutory instrument setting the price.
Renewal with benchmark evidence requires market benchmark data obtained within the previous 12 months, from an independent source such as a benchmarking provider, a market index, or a documented parallel quotation, showing that the incumbent price remains competitive.
Limited market response requires the invitation and response record described above.

Approval Routing

The exception is approved one band above the approval band of the underlying spend under the Global Procurement Policy. A €40,000 requirement, ordinarily approved by the Category Manager, therefore requires VP Procurement approval of the exception. The approver must be independent of the requesting business function. Procurement Governance reviews every exception above €250,000 before the approver receives it, and may return the request for further evidence.

Duration and Renewal Limits

An approved exception is valid for a maximum of 12 months or for the duration of the specific award, whichever is shorter. A requirement may not be renewed under a sourcing exception more than twice consecutively. On the second renewal the buyer must record a plan and a date for a competitive event or a Category Council decision to designate the supplier as strategic and single-sourced by design.

Record Keeping and Audit Trail

The following must exist in Ariba Sourcing for every award above €25,000: the requirement document issued to suppliers, the invitation list with dates, the bids received or the exception form, the comparison or evaluation record, the award recommendation, and the approval evidence. Records are retained for seven years. Internal Audit samples awards quarterly and tests whether the exception ground claimed is supported by the evidence attached, and the most common finding is a sole-source claim supported only by an assertion.

Reporting

Procurement Governance publishes an exception dashboard quarterly, broken down by category, business unit, exception ground, and value, and flags any business unit whose exception rate exceeds 15% of addressable spend.

title: Standard Operating Procedure — Invoice Exception and Three-Way Match Resolution
section_headings: Goods Receipt and Invoice Receipt Reconciliation
text:
Purpose

This procedure defines how invoices are matched, which variances are tolerated automatically, how blocked invoices are investigated and cleared, and who is accountable at each step. It applies to all purchase-order-based invoices across Vantera entities processed in SAP S/4HANA.

The Three-Way Match

An invoice is matched against three independent records: the purchase order, which represents what was authorised and at what price; the goods receipt or service entry sheet, which represents what was actually delivered and accepted; and the invoice itself, which represents what the supplier is charging. The control value of the three-way match comes from the fact that the three records are created by different people at different times. Where the same person raises the requisition, confirms receipt, and approves the invoice, the control provides no assurance, which is why segregation of duties is enforced at each step.

Automatic Tolerances

An invoice posts automatically without human intervention where it is within all of the following tolerances. Price variance up to and including 3% of the purchase order line value. Quantity variance up to and including 5 units, provided the variance does not exceed the ordered quantity. Absolute variance up to and including €50 per invoice regardless of percentage, which prevents trivial rounding and freight differences from consuming buyer time. Date variance where the invoice date precedes the goods receipt date by no more than 3 calendar days. Any invoice breaching one or more of these tolerances is blocked for review and does not pay.

Block Types and Ownership

Price block, raised where the invoice unit price exceeds the purchase order price beyond tolerance, is owned by the buyer who placed the order. Quantity block, raised where the invoiced quantity exceeds the received quantity, is owned by the receiving location. Goods receipt missing, raised where an invoice arrives with no corresponding receipt, is owned by the requester or the site goods-in team. Purchase order missing or closed, raised where the invoice references no valid open order, is owned by the requesting manager. Tax and compliance block, raised where the VAT treatment or entity details are wrong, is owned by Accounts Payable and normally resolved by requesting a corrected invoice.

Resolution Timescales

Blocked invoices must be actioned within 5 business days of assignment. An invoice blocked for more than 10 business days is escalated to the buyer's line manager, and one blocked for more than 20 business days is escalated to the Category Director and reported in the monthly Procure-to-Pay review. Ageing matters because a blocked invoice frequently means the supplier has not been paid for goods Vantera has already consumed, which creates both a supplier relationship problem and an unrecorded liability.

Investigating a Price Block

The buyer first checks whether the purchase order reflects the current contracted price, since the most common root cause is an indexation or price change that was agreed commercially but never updated on the order. Where the contract price has changed, the buyer amends the purchase order and the invoice reposts. Where the supplier has invoiced above the contracted price, the buyer raises a query with the supplier, and the invoice is rejected or a credit note is requested. Where a genuine one-off surcharge applies, such as an out-of-hours delivery agreed in advance, the buyer documents the approval and amends the order. A buyer may not simply raise the purchase order value to clear a block without establishing why the price differs, and Internal Audit tests specifically for this pattern.

Quantity and Receipt Variances

Where the invoice exceeds the receipt, the receiving location confirms whether goods were delivered but not receipted, delivered short, or damaged and rejected. Where goods were delivered but not receipted, the receipt is posted with the actual delivery date, not the current date, because posting date drives the accrual. Where a short delivery is confirmed, the supplier is asked for a credit note and the invoice is paid only for the quantity received. Repeated short deliveries are recorded as a delivery performance issue on the supplier scorecard.

Goods Receipt and Invoice Receipt Reconciliation

The goods-received not-invoiced account is reviewed monthly. Items older than 90 days are investigated, because they usually indicate either a receipt posted against the wrong order, a service that was completed but never invoiced, or an order that should have been closed. Unresolved items older than 180 days are written back with Finance approval and a documented reason.

Duplicate Invoices

Duplicate detection runs on supplier, invoice number, gross amount, and invoice date. A common false positive arises where a supplier reuses invoice numbers across legal entities or resubmits a corrected invoice under the same number. Accounts Payable resolves duplicates before payment and never after, because recovering a duplicate payment depends entirely on the supplier's willingness to return it.

Supplier Performance Link

Suppliers generating a high rate of invoice exceptions are addressed through the supplier performance process. A supplier whose first-time-right invoice rate falls below 90% over a rolling quarter is raised in the next business review with a corrective action, since invoice quality is a controllable supplier behaviour, and root causes are usually incorrect purchase order references, outdated price files, or invoices raised before delivery.

Reporting

Procure-to-Pay reports weekly on blocked invoice volume and value by block type, ageing buckets, and the top ten blocked invoices by value, and monthly on first-time-right rate by supplier and by business unit.

title: Standard Operating Procedure — Supplier Bank Detail Changes and Payment Fraud Prevention
section_headings: Additional Controls for High-Value or High-Risk Changes
If a Fraudulent Payment Is Suspected
text:
Purpose

This procedure defines the controls applied whenever a supplier's bank details are created or changed. Business email compromise and invoice redirection fraud are the highest-frequency financial crime risks facing procure-to-pay, and almost every successful case follows the same pattern: a plausible email, an urgent tone, and a change of bank account processed without independent verification.

Scope

This procedure applies to the creation of bank details for a new supplier, any change to an existing supplier's bank account, changes to a supplier's remittance email address, and any request to make a one-off payment to an account other than the one held in the supplier master.

Who May Initiate a Change

A bank detail change may only be initiated by the supplier through the Ariba Supplier Information Management portal, using the supplier's own registered portal credentials. Changes requested by email, by telephone, on a letterhead, or through a Vantera employee acting on the supplier's behalf are not accepted, and the requester is redirected to the portal. Vantera buyers may not enter bank details on behalf of a supplier under any circumstances, including where the supplier claims it cannot access the portal.

Mandatory Callback Verification

Every bank detail change requires an independent callback before it is activated. The verification analyst calls the supplier using a telephone number obtained from the supplier master record as it existed before the change request, or from the supplier's official public registration record. The number may not be taken from the change request, from the invoice, from an email signature, from a covering letter, or from a website link supplied in the request, because all of these are controlled by the party making the request. The analyst speaks to a named finance contact, confirms the change was genuinely initiated by the supplier, and confirms the last four digits of the new account together with the account name.

Recording the Verification

The analyst records the date and time of the call, the number dialled, the source of that number, the name and role of the person spoken to, and the confirmation outcome. This record is attached to the change request in SAP MDG-S. A change may not be activated on the basis of a voicemail, an email confirmation, or a call to a number that could not be independently sourced.

Dual Approval and Payment Hold

After successful callback verification, the change requires approval by a second person in the Supplier Master team who was not involved in the verification. On activation, an automatic 24-hour hold is applied to all payments to that supplier, which provides a final window in which an anomaly can surface. The first payment to the new account is flagged for review, and the buyer is notified so that an unexpected change becomes visible to the person who knows the relationship.

Additional Controls for High-Value or High-Risk Changes

Where the supplier's average monthly payment value exceeds €250,000, or where the change is to an account in a country different from the supplier's registered country, a second independent verification is required through a different channel, such as a call to a different named contact or written confirmation on the supplier's registered domain combined with a bank-issued account confirmation letter. Changes to an account held by a payment intermediary, a factoring company, or a third party require Legal review and a written assignment or factoring notice from the supplier.

Red Flags

Escalate immediately, and do not process, where the request conveys urgency tied to a payment run or period end, where the requester resists callback verification or supplies only a mobile number, where the email domain differs subtly from the known domain, for example by a transposed character or an added hyphen, where the new account is in a different country or in a name that does not match the supplier's legal name, where a change arrives shortly after a genuine contact change at the supplier, or where the request references a real invoice number that suggests the requester has visibility of correspondence.

If a Fraudulent Payment Is Suspected

Contact Treasury immediately to attempt recall, because the probability of recovery falls sharply after the first 24 hours. Notify Group Compliance and Group Security, preserve all emails and headers without forwarding them in a way that alters them, do not alert the suspected fraudulent contact, and notify the genuine supplier through a known channel so that they can check whether their own systems are compromised. A confirmed or attempted fraud is reported to the Audit Committee and triggers a review of whether the control failed or was bypassed.

Assurance

The Supplier Master team reports monthly on the number of bank detail changes processed, the number rejected, the number of callbacks that failed verification, and any suspected fraud attempts. Internal Audit tests a sample of changes annually against the evidence requirements in this procedure.

title: Standard Operating Procedure — Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order Intake
section_headings: Changes to an Issued Purchase Order
text:
Purpose

This procedure describes how a business need becomes an approved purchase order, the service levels at each stage, and the routing rules that determine whether a request is handled through self-service, through a buyer, or through a full sourcing event.

Channels

Vantera operates three buying channels, and choosing the right one is the single biggest driver of cycle time. Catalogue buying covers pre-negotiated goods and services available in the Ariba Buying catalogue, where the price, supplier, and terms are already agreed; these requests require only budget owner approval and convert to a purchase order automatically. Guided buying covers requirements that are not in a catalogue but fall under an existing framework agreement, where the system routes the requester through a structured form and applies the contracted terms. Sourcing covers requirements with no existing agreement, which are routed to a Category Manager for a competitive event or a sourcing exception.

Purchasing Cards

Purchasing cards are available for low-value, low-risk, non-recurring purchases where no catalogue exists, subject to a single-transaction limit of €2,500 and a monthly limit of €10,000. Purchasing cards may not be used for services performed on Vantera premises, for anything requiring a contract, for capital items, for contingent labour, for software or subscriptions of any value, or to split a larger purchase into card-sized transactions. Cardholders reconcile transactions with receipts within 10 business days.

Raising a Requisition

The requester creates the requisition in Ariba Buying with a clear description of what is being bought and why, the correct cost centre and general ledger account, the delivery location and required date, the commodity code, and any supporting documents such as a quotation, statement of work, or business case. Requisitions for services must include a statement of work with defined deliverables, acceptance criteria, and milestone dates, because a service requisition described only as consultancy support cannot be receipted objectively and later becomes a disputed invoice.

Categorisation and Routing Service Level

Procurement Operations assigns an unrouted requisition to the correct category within 2 business days. Where a requisition is incorrectly categorised, it is reassigned rather than rejected, and the requester is informed. Miscategorisation matters beyond routing, because commodity codes drive spend analytics, ESG assessment scope, and category strategy.

Approval Flow

The requisition follows the approval bands in the Global Procurement Policy, and the system derives the required approvers from the total committed value, the commodity code, and the cost centre. Additional approvers are added automatically where the request involves personal data processing, which adds the Data Protection Officer, software or cloud services, which adds Enterprise Architecture and InfoSec Procurement, contingent labour, which adds Human Resources, capital expenditure, which adds the capital approval workflow, or a new supplier, which adds the Supplier Risk Office. Approvers act within 3 business days, and requests pending more than 5 business days are escalated automatically to the approver's line manager.

Purchase Order Issue

Once fully approved, the purchase order is issued to the supplier through the Ariba Network. The purchase order is the commercial instruction, and it is the document against which the supplier may begin work. Buyers must not send a preliminary confirmation to a supplier, such as an email stating that the order is coming, because a supplier that begins work on that basis is entitled to argue that a contract was formed outside the approval process.

Indicative Cycle Times

Catalogue purchase: 1 business day from requisition to purchase order where approvals are prompt. Guided buying under an existing framework: 3 to 5 business days. Three-bid sourcing event: 4 to 6 weeks from complete requirement to award. Formal request for proposal: 8 to 12 weeks from launch to award, plus contracting time. Requesters are advised of the realistic lead time at intake, because unrealistic expectations at the start are the most common reason a requirement later arrives as an emergency.

Changes to an Issued Purchase Order

Scope, price, and quantity changes require a purchase order amendment approved at the band applicable to the revised total committed value. A change that increases the value into a higher band requires the higher band approver, not merely the original approver. Amendments are made before the supplier performs the additional work.

Closing Orders

Purchase orders are closed once fully received and invoiced. Orders with no activity for 12 months are closed automatically after notification to the requester, releasing the commitment from the budget.

title: Standard Operating Procedure — Supplier Segmentation, Performance Reviews and Scorecards
text:
Purpose

This procedure defines how suppliers are segmented, how often performance is reviewed, what is measured, and what happens when performance falls below the required standard. Its aim is to make supplier management proportionate, so that management effort is concentrated where value and risk actually sit.

Segmentation Model

Every active supplier is assigned a tier annually, based on the previous 12 months of spend and on a criticality assessment.

Tier 1 strategic (annual spend above €500,000, or business-critical regardless of spend): quarterly business review chaired by the Category Manager, an executive sponsor on both sides, a joint improvement plan, and an on-site audit every 24 months.
Tier 2 managed (annual spend between €100,000 and €500,000): semi-annual performance review, an annual self-assessment questionnaire, and a documented improvement action list.
Tier 3 transactional (annual spend below €100,000 and not business-critical): annual scorecard produced from system data only, with intervention by exception.

Business-critical means that a supplier interruption would stop production, prevent shipment to a customer, breach a regulatory obligation, or interrupt a system supporting a critical process. A supplier with modest spend can therefore be Tier 1, and a single-source ingredient supplier at €200,000 of annual spend is a common example.

Scorecard Dimensions and Weightings

Scorecards use a consistent 100-point model so that results are comparable across a category.

Quality (30 points): defect rate, non-conformance reports, complaint volume, and audit findings.
Delivery (25 points): on-time in-full performance, lead time adherence, and order fill rate.
Cost (20 points): cost reduction delivered against the agreed baseline, price stability, invoice accuracy, and adherence to the agreed indexation mechanism.
Service and responsiveness (15 points): query response time, issue resolution time, quality of account management, and flexibility on urgent requests.
Sustainability and compliance (10 points): EcoVadis score, evidence of certifications maintained, audit corrective action closure, and Scope 3 data provision.

A score of 70 or above is a pass. A score between 60 and 69 requires a documented improvement action with a named owner and a review date. A score below 60 requires a formal corrective action plan submitted by the supplier within 20 business days, with milestones and a re-measurement point at 90 days.

Data Sources

Scorecard data is drawn from system records first, and from opinion only where no system record exists. On-time in-full performance is calculated from goods receipt dates against the confirmed delivery date on the purchase order, not against the date the requester wished for. Invoice accuracy is calculated from the first-time-right rate in the invoice exception process. Quality data comes from the non-conformance system. Only the service and responsiveness dimension is stakeholder-rated, and it is collected through a short structured survey of at least three named stakeholders to avoid a single strong opinion dominating.

Running a Quarterly Business Review

The agenda covers performance against the scorecard with agreed data shared in advance, open corrective actions, the commercial position including savings delivered and the pipeline, risk topics including business continuity, cyber, and sustainability, innovation and improvement proposals from the supplier, and a forward view of demand. Vantera's own performance is also reviewed, including on-time payment rate, forecast accuracy, and responsiveness on approvals, because most persistent supplier performance issues have a shared root cause. Minutes and actions are recorded in Ariba SIM within 5 business days, with owners and dates on both sides.

Escalation and Consequence

Where a corrective action plan fails at the 90-day re-measurement, the Category Manager escalates to the Category Director, who agrees one of the following: an extended plan with executive sponsorship, a reduction in allocated volume, suspension from new sourcing events, or termination and resourcing. Where contractual service credits apply, they are applied consistently rather than waived informally, because inconsistent enforcement undermines the contract in any later dispute. Any decision to waive a credit requires Category Director approval and a recorded reason.

Recognising Good Performance

Suppliers scoring above 90 for four consecutive quarters are eligible for preferred supplier status, which carries first refusal on relevant new demand, participation in early innovation briefings, and a joint case study where appropriate. Recognition is genuinely useful commercially, because it gives the supplier's account team an internal argument for continuing to invest in the relationship.

Annual Re-Segmentation and Data Hygiene

Tiers are recalculated annually using the previous 12 months of spend plus the criticality assessment, and a change of tier is communicated to the supplier along with what will change in the review cadence. Suppliers with no purchase order activity for 24 months are set to inactive under the supplier onboarding policy, and their scorecards are archived rather than deleted, so that history is available if the supplier is later reactivated.

title: Standard Operating Procedure — Contract Renewal, Expiry and Evergreen Management
section_headings: Why Notice Dates Are Managed Actively
text:
Purpose

This procedure defines how contract expiries and renewals are managed so that Vantera never renews by accident, never loses a service because a notice date passed unnoticed, and never renews without knowing whether the commercial terms are still competitive.

Why Notice Dates Are Managed Actively

A missed notice date is one of the few procurement errors that cannot be corrected after the fact. Where a contract renews automatically because notice was not served in time, Vantera is committed for a further term at terms it did not choose. The two most common causes are a contract that was never loaded into Ariba Contracts, and a renewal alert that was sent to an owner who had changed role.

The Renewal Calendar

Every contract in Ariba Contracts carries an expiry date, a notice period, and a calculated notice deadline. The Contract Management Office issues automated alerts to the contract owner and the Category Manager at 180 days, 120 days, 90 days, and 30 days before the notice deadline, and a final alert to the Category Director at 15 days. The 120-day alert is the operative one: it is the point at which a renewal decision process must formally start, because it leaves enough time to run a competitive event where the decision is not to renew.

Renewal Decision Path

At 120 days the Category Manager assesses current performance from the most recent scorecards, whether the requirement is still needed at the same volume, whether the pricing remains competitive against the market, whether the terms remain compliant with current policy, particularly on security, data protection, and responsible sourcing, and whether the supplier's risk profile has changed. The outcome is one of four decisions: renew as is, renew with renegotiated terms, run a competitive event, or exit and terminate. Each outcome is recorded in Ariba Contracts with the supporting evidence.

Renewing Without Competition

A renewal without a competitive event is permitted under the Competitive Sourcing and Bidding Policy where documented market benchmark evidence obtained within the previous 12 months shows that current pricing remains competitive. Acceptable evidence includes a benchmarking report from an independent provider, a documented parallel quotation for a comparable scope, a published market index movement applied to a transparent cost model, or a peer-group price comparison from a category benchmarking service. A supplier's own assertion that its pricing is market-leading is not benchmark evidence.

Serving Notice

Notice must be served in the manner the contract requires, which usually means written notice to a named contractual address, and frequently requires recorded delivery rather than email. The buyer checks the notices clause rather than assuming, because notice served by email where the contract requires post is capable of being challenged. A copy of the notice and proof of delivery are filed against the contract record. Where the intention is to renegotiate rather than exit, notice to terminate may still be served to preserve optionality, and this should be explained to the supplier directly to avoid unnecessary relationship damage.

Auto-Renewal and Evergreen Contracts

Automatic renewal is permitted only where Vantera holds a right to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice or less. Where a legacy contract contains an evergreen term without such a right, the Contract Management Office records it on the exceptions register and it is renegotiated at the next opportunity. Software and subscription agreements deserve particular attention, because auto-renewal combined with an annual uplift is the standard commercial model and licence counts frequently drift upward between renewals.

Expiry Without Renewal

Where a contract will expire without replacement, the Category Manager confirms that demand has genuinely ceased, that outstanding purchase orders will complete before expiry, that the supplier record is set to no new orders, that any data return or deletion obligation is executed and evidenced, and that any equipment, tooling, or intellectual property held by the supplier is returned.

Transition to a New Supplier

Where a competitive event results in a change of supplier, the exit assistance obligations in the outgoing contract are invoked in writing, a transition plan with dates and named owners is agreed with both suppliers, and the overlap period is costed and approved. Data return and deletion are evidenced by a written confirmation from the outgoing supplier, and the final invoice is not paid until that confirmation is received.

Reporting and Data Quality

The Contract Management Office reports monthly on contracts expiring within 180 days, contracts renewed without benchmark evidence, missed notice deadlines, and contracts in the repository with missing expiry or notice metadata. Metadata completeness is treated as a control, because an alert cannot fire on a date the system does not hold.

title: Standard Operating Procedure — Supplier Risk Incidents and Business Continuity Escalation
text:
Purpose

This procedure defines how a supplier risk event is reported, triaged, escalated, and closed, and what pre-emptive controls apply to single-source and business-critical suppliers. It covers financial distress, operational failure, cyber and data incidents, quality and food safety events, sanctions and compliance events, and natural or geopolitical disruption.

Reporting an Event

Anyone who becomes aware of a supplier risk event reports it to the Supplier Risk Office the same working day through the risk event form in Ariba SIM. Reports are made on suspicion and do not require confirmation, because early low-confidence information is far more useful than late certainty. The report captures the supplier, the site or service affected, what is known and when it was learned, the products or services at risk, and the immediate operational impact if known.

Severity Triage

The Supplier Risk Office triages within 4 working hours and assigns a severity.

Severity 1 (critical): production stoppage, customer supply failure, confirmed data breach affecting personal data, a food safety or product recall event, or a sanctions match on an active supplier. Response is immediate, a crisis call is convened within 2 hours, and the Category Director, the business unit leadership, and Group Compliance are notified.
Severity 2 (major): significant disruption with a workaround available, financial distress indicators such as a credit rating downgrade or filing for protection, a security incident without confirmed data loss, or a failed regulatory inspection. Response within 1 business day, with a mitigation plan within 3 business days.
