Severity 3 (moderate): service degradation, a missed milestone, a lapsed certification, or an adverse media report. Response within 3 business days, managed through the normal performance process.

Immediate Actions for Severity 1

The crisis call confirms the factual position, quantifies exposure in terms of days of cover and affected volumes, identifies alternative supply including qualified alternates and available inventory, decides on customer and regulatory communication, and appoints a single named incident owner. Where a data or security incident is involved, the information security incident process runs in parallel and the 72-hour personal data breach notification clock is assumed to have started at the point Vantera became aware, unless legal advice determines otherwise. Where a sanctions match is involved, all payments and orders to the supplier are blocked immediately pending Compliance disposition.

Financial Distress Indicators

Dun and Bradstreet alerts feed the supplier master daily, and the following are treated as triggers for a Severity 2 review: a failure score deterioration of two bands or more, a county court judgment or equivalent, a late filing of statutory accounts, a change of auditor combined with a qualified opinion, redundancy announcements affecting the servicing site, and requests from the supplier to shorten payment terms or to receive prepayment. A request for accelerated payment is frequently the earliest signal Vantera receives, and it is treated as risk information rather than only as a commercial negotiation.

Single-Source and Business-Critical Suppliers

For every single-source item classified as business-critical, the Category Manager maintains a continuity record containing the identified risk, the days of cover held as inventory, a named qualified or qualifiable alternative supplier, the estimated requalification time, and the tooling or intellectual property position. Continuity records are reviewed annually, and any item with more than 12 weeks of requalification time and less than 4 weeks of cover is escalated to the Category Council for a dual-sourcing or strategic-stock decision.

Force Majeure Claims

A force majeure notice from a supplier is acknowledged in writing without admission, and Legal reviews whether the claimed event falls within the contractual definition, whether the notice complies with the contractual requirements as to timing and content, and what mitigation the supplier is obliged to attempt. Vantera requires evidence of the event's actual effect on the supplier's ability to perform, and requires the supplier to allocate available capacity fairly rather than preferring other customers. Price increases requested under the label of force majeure are treated as commercial renegotiation and are handled through the normal negotiation and approval process.

Closure and Learning

An event is closed when the operational impact is resolved, corrective actions are agreed with owners and dates, and any contractual consequence such as service credits, recovery of costs, or a termination decision has been actioned. Severity 1 and Severity 2 events receive a written post-incident review within 15 business days covering root cause, what was detected late and why, and what control change would prevent recurrence. Findings are fed into category strategies and into the annual continuity record review.

Reporting

The Supplier Risk Office reports monthly on open events by severity, the top ten supplier risks by exposure, continuity record coverage for business-critical items, and overdue corrective actions.

title: Standard Operating Procedure — Emergency, Retrospective and Off-Catalogue Purchases
text:
Purpose

This procedure defines what qualifies as an emergency purchase, how work may lawfully begin before a purchase order exists, how a retrospective purchase order is raised and approved, and how unauthorised commitments are regularised and reported.

What Qualifies as an Emergency

An emergency is a situation where a delay would cause a safety risk to people, a food safety or product quality risk, a regulatory or legal breach, a production line stoppage or imminent stoppage, a failure to supply a customer order, or a material security or data protection risk. Poor planning is not an emergency. A deadline that has been known for weeks, an expiring budget, an approver who is on leave, and a contract that was allowed to lapse are not emergencies, and treating them as such devalues the mechanism for the situations that genuinely need it.

Authorising Emergency Work

Emergency work may begin on the verbal approval of a manager who holds the approval band appropriate to the estimated total committed value under the Global Procurement Policy. The approving manager must be told the estimated value at the time of approval, and where the value is uncertain the higher end of the estimate governs which band applies. The requester records the emergency reason, the estimated spend, the supplier name, and the name of the approving manager within 2 business days, and a retrospective purchase order is raised within 5 business days.

Additional Constraints During an Emergency

Even in an emergency, a supplier must exist in the supplier master with completed onboarding before any payment can be made, and sanctions screening may not be skipped. Where an unlisted supplier is genuinely the only option, expedited onboarding is requested with VP Procurement approval, which is completed within 3 business days. Emergency purchases involving personal data processing still require a data processing agreement before go-live, and emergency purchases requiring work on Vantera premises still require evidence of insurance and, where applicable, a safety induction. These are not administrative preferences: they are the controls whose absence turns an operational emergency into a legal or safety incident.

Raising a Retrospective Purchase Order

A retrospective purchase order is raised in Ariba Buying using the retrospective flag, which routes it through a distinct approval path. The requisition must state the date the work started or the goods were delivered, the reason the order was not raised in advance, the name of the person who authorised the commitment, and whether the situation met the emergency definition above. Where the situation did not meet the emergency definition, the commitment is recorded as an unauthorised commitment.

Approval of Unauthorised Commitments

An unauthorised commitment is approved one band above the band that would ordinarily have applied to the value, under the Global Procurement Policy. The approving manager is expected to consider whether the commitment should be honoured, and in practice it usually must be, because the supplier has already performed in good faith and Vantera's legal exposure is unaffected by an internal control failure. The purpose of the higher approval is visibility and accountability, not obstruction.

Off-Catalogue and Maverick Spend

Off-catalogue purchasing means buying outside an available catalogue or framework where one exists, usually resulting in a higher price and non-contracted terms. Where a requester submits an off-catalogue request for an item available in the catalogue, Procurement Operations redirects the request rather than processing it, unless there is a documented reason such as an urgent stock-out at the catalogue supplier. Repeated off-catalogue buying by a cost centre is addressed with the budget owner, because it is normally a symptom of a catalogue gap, a usability problem, or a lead-time expectation that the standard channel does not meet.

Prohibited Practices

Splitting a commitment across multiple requisitions to stay below an approval band, backdating a requisition or a goods receipt, raising a purchase order to a supplier different from the one that performed the work, describing a requisition generically to avoid a category routing rule, and issuing a purchase order after an invoice has been received solely in order to clear the invoice without investigating the underlying commitment are all control breaches and are reported to Internal Audit.

Reporting and Trend Management

Procurement Operations reports monthly on emergency purchase volume and value by cost centre and category, retrospective purchase order rate, and unauthorised commitment count. A cost centre with more than six emergency purchases in a rolling 12-month period is subject to a process review with the budget owner, and the review looks for the underlying cause, most commonly an expired contract, an unmanaged demand pattern, or a catalogue gap, rather than treating each instance in isolation.

title: Master Services Agreement Summary — Acme Logistics S.L. (MSA-ACM-2024-018)
text:
Parties and Structure

This is a summary of the master services agreement MSA-ACM-2024-018 between Vantera Iberia, S.L.U. and Acme Logistics S.L., supplier identifier SUP-100482, registered in Madrid. The agreement was awarded following RFP-EMEA-2025-0132 and comprises the master agreement, Schedule 1 scope of services, Schedule 2 rate card, Schedule 3 service levels, Schedule 4 data protection terms, and Schedule 5 sustainability commitments. The order of precedence places the master agreement above the schedules, and the schedules above any purchase order terms.

Scope of Services

Acme Logistics S.L. provides warehouse-to-store distribution services for Vantera in Spain and Portugal, covering ambient and chilled product from the Vantera distribution centres in Guadalajara and Valencia to approximately 1,850 retail delivery points. Services include outbound transport, cross-docking, returns collection, pallet management, and delivery confirmation with electronic proof of delivery transmitted within 4 hours of delivery. Frozen product below minus 18 degrees Celsius is expressly out of scope and is served under a separate arrangement.

Term and Renewal

The agreement has an initial term of three years, effective from 2024-05-12 and expiring on 2027-05-12. Renewal is not automatic. Either party may renew by written agreement, and where Vantera does not wish to renew, written notice of non-renewal must be served no later than 90 days before 2027-05-12, which sets a notice deadline of 2027-02-11. Notice must be served in writing to the registered address specified in the notices clause; email notice alone does not satisfy the clause. The Contract Management Office alert schedule places the operative renewal decision point at 120 days before the notice deadline.

Service Levels

The primary service level is on-time delivery of 98.5%, measured monthly as the percentage of delivery lines arriving within the agreed delivery window at the store, excluding delays caused by Vantera or by a valid force majeure event. Supporting service levels are order fill rate of 99.2%, electronic proof of delivery transmission within 4 hours for 99% of deliveries, claims acknowledgement within 2 business days, and claims resolution within 20 business days. Acme provides a monthly key performance indicator report by the fifth business day of the following month, broken down by depot, by region, and by delivery window.

Service Credits

Service credits become payable where the on-time delivery service level is missed in two consecutive monthly measurement periods. The credit is 2% of the monthly charges for the second consecutive missed period, rising to 4% for a third consecutive missed period and 6% for a fourth and each subsequent consecutive missed period, and the credit resets once a compliant month is achieved. Service credits are Vantera's exclusive financial remedy for service level failure, but they do not limit the right to terminate for material breach, and they do not apply to claims for loss or damage to goods, which are handled under the claims and liability provisions.

Pricing and Fuel Surcharge

Pricing is per pallet by lane and by delivery window, set out in the Schedule 2 rate card. Base rates are fixed for the first 24 months of the term and are then subject to annual review linked to the Spanish transport labour cost index, capped at the lower of the index movement or 3.5%. A separate fuel surcharge mechanism applies monthly, indexed to the published Spanish gasoil price, with a deadband of plus or minus 3%: the surcharge adjusts only where the monthly average gasoil price moves outside that band relative to the baseline, and the adjustment is applied to the fuel-attributable portion of the rate, stated in Schedule 2 as 22% of the base rate. Acme must provide the index reference and the calculation with each surcharge adjustment, and Vantera has open-book audit rights over the calculation.

Liability, Insurance and Claims

Each party's aggregate liability is capped at 150% of the charges paid in the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, with the standard uncapped carve-outs for data protection breach, intellectual property infringement, death or personal injury, fraud, and wilful misconduct. Liability for loss of or damage to goods in transit is governed by the CMR Convention where applicable, and Acme maintains goods-in-transit cover of €2,000,000 per vehicle and general third-party liability of €5,000,000 per occurrence. Claims for shortage or damage must be notified within 7 calendar days of delivery.

Data Protection and Sustainability

Acme processes limited personal data, being store contact details and driver identification data, under the Schedule 4 data processing terms. Under Schedule 5, Acme reports monthly fuel consumption and calculated CO2 emissions per pallet delivered, has committed to converting 30% of the dedicated fleet serving Vantera to low-emission vehicles by 2027-12-31, and maintains an EcoVadis score of at least 45, currently assessed at 58.

Governance and Termination

A monthly operational review is held with the Iberia logistics team, and a quarterly business review is held with the Category Manager under the Tier 1 supplier segmentation. Vantera may terminate for convenience on 90 days' written notice, for material breach not remedied within 30 days, and immediately on insolvency or change of control to a competitor. On termination, Acme provides transition assistance for up to 90 days at the Schedule 2 rates, and returns all Vantera pallets, equipment, and data.

title: Data Processing Agreement Summary — Northstar Analytics Ltd. (DPA-NST-2025-004)
text:
Parties and Relationship

This is a summary of the data processing agreement DPA-NST-2025-004, which forms Schedule 4 to master services agreement MSA-NST-2025-004 between Vantera Group N.V. and Northstar Analytics Ltd., supplier identifier SUP-100915, registered in London. Vantera acts as controller and Northstar acts as processor. Where Northstar processes data for its own product telemetry, it acts as an independent controller, and that processing is limited to the categories expressly listed in Annex 3 and may not include Vantera commercial data.

Permitted Processing

Northstar Analytics Ltd. may process sales transaction data, inventory and stock movement data, supplier performance data, and store operational data for the sole purpose of providing the commercial analytics and dashboard reporting services described in the statement of work. Personal data in scope is limited to business contact details of Vantera employees and supplier contacts, and store colleague identifiers used for operational reporting. Consumer personal data is out of scope and must not be transferred to Northstar under this agreement. Processing for any purpose beyond the documented instructions requires prior written approval from the Vantera Data Protection Officer.

Prohibition on Model Training

Northstar may not use Vantera data to train, fine-tune, evaluate, benchmark, or otherwise improve any machine learning or artificial intelligence model without prior written approval from Vantera. This prohibition expressly extends to aggregated, anonymised, and pseudonymised derivatives of Vantera data, and to the use of Vantera data as evaluation or test data. Where Northstar wishes to use aggregated cross-customer benchmarks that include Vantera data, it must obtain written approval identifying the specific dataset, the purpose, and the retention period. Approval given for one purpose does not extend to another.

Sub-Processors

Northstar maintains a list of approved sub-processors in Annex 2. Any addition or replacement of a sub-processor must be notified to Vantera at least 30 days before the sub-processor begins processing Vantera data. Vantera may object within 20 days of notification on reasonable data protection grounds, and where the objection cannot be resolved, Vantera may terminate the affected services without penalty. Northstar remains fully liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors. The currently approved sub-processors are the cloud hosting provider for the Dublin region, a transactional email provider, and an out-of-hours support provider operating from the United Kingdom.

Location of Processing and Transfers

All Vantera data is hosted in the European Union in the Dublin region, with backups replicated within the European Union only. Support access from the United Kingdom is permitted under the UK adequacy decision. Any transfer to a third country requires prior written approval, Standard Contractual Clauses, and a documented transfer impact assessment. Northstar must notify Vantera before any change to the hosting region, and a change without notice is a material breach.

Security Measures

Northstar maintains ISO 27001 certification covering the production environment and provides an annual SOC 2 Type II report. Data is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.3 and at rest using AES-256. Access to Vantera data is restricted to named personnel on a least-privilege basis, with access reviews performed quarterly and multi-factor authentication enforced. An independent penetration test is performed annually and the executive summary is shared with Vantera within 30 days of completion.

Breach Notification

Northstar must notify Vantera of any personal data breach or any security incident affecting Vantera data without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware. This is stricter than the 72-hour floor in the Vantera information security policy, and the contractual 24-hour period prevails. The notification must describe the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of data subjects and records affected, the likely consequences, and the measures taken or proposed. Northstar must cooperate fully with any regulatory notification Vantera is required to make.

Audit and Assurance

Vantera may audit Northstar's compliance on 10 business days' written notice, no more than once in any 12-month period unless a breach is suspected or a regulator requires it. Northstar may satisfy an audit request by providing the SOC 2 Type II report and completing the Vantera security questionnaire, unless Vantera reasonably requires a direct audit.

Return and Deletion of Data

On termination or expiry, Northstar must return Vantera data in a documented, machine-readable, non-proprietary format on request, and must delete all remaining copies within 45 days of termination, including copies held by sub-processors. Backup copies may persist within the documented backup rotation for a maximum of 90 days, after which they are irreversibly deleted. Northstar must provide written certification of deletion signed by an officer. Data may not be withheld on the basis of a commercial dispute.

Term and Precedence

The data processing agreement runs coterminously with MSA-NST-2025-004, which expires on 2028-05-31. Where the data processing agreement conflicts with any other document, the data processing agreement prevails on matters of data protection.

title: Supply Agreement Summary — Batavia Packaging B.V. (SA-BAT-2025-007)
text:
Parties and Scope

This is a summary of supply agreement SA-BAT-2025-007 between Vantera Group N.V., contracting on behalf of its European manufacturing entities, and Batavia Packaging B.V., supplier identifier SUP-100311, registered in Rotterdam. Batavia supplies corrugated shipping cases, folding cartons, and flexible film laminates to Vantera plants in the Netherlands, Germany, Spain, and Poland. Article and specification detail is held in Schedule 1, which is maintained as a controlled document and updated by written amendment only.

Term and Volume Commitment

The agreement runs from 2025-10-01 to 2028-09-30. Vantera commits to a minimum annual volume of 18,000 tonnes across the article portfolio, with a flexibility band of plus or minus 15% measured annually. Volumes below the lower bound trigger a good-faith review of the rate card rather than an automatic price increase, and volumes above the upper bound entitle Vantera to request additional capacity, which Batavia must use reasonable endeavours to provide within 90 days. Article-level forecasts are provided monthly on a rolling 12-month horizon, with the first 8 weeks firm and weeks 9 to 13 within a 20% variation tolerance.

Price Indexation

Prices are quoted per thousand units by article and are reviewed quarterly through a transparent indexation mechanism rather than negotiation. The corrugated portfolio is indexed to the published European testliner and fluting price index, and the flexible portfolio is indexed to the ICIS polyethylene contract price for north-west Europe. Indexation applies only to the raw material component of the price, which is fixed in Schedule 2 at 62% for corrugated articles and 71% for flexible articles, with the balance representing conversion, waste, energy, and margin, which are fixed for the first 24 months. A deadband of plus or minus 2% applies: an index movement within the deadband does not trigger a price change and is carried forward to the next quarterly review. Price changes require 60 days' written notice, take effect on the first day of the following quarter, and must be supported by the published index values and the calculation. Vantera holds open-book audit rights over the cost model and may audit the indexation calculation once per contract year on 10 business days' notice.

Energy Surcharge

A separate energy surcharge mechanism was introduced by amendment 2 with effect from 2026-04-01, indexed to the Dutch TTF gas benchmark, applying only to the conversion element and capped at 4% of the total article price in any 12-month period. The surcharge is reviewed quarterly alongside the raw material indexation and expires on 2027-09-30 unless renewed by written agreement.

Quality and Specification

Batavia manufactures to the specifications in Schedule 1, holds BRCGS Packaging Materials certification at Grade AA for all supplying sites, and complies with EU Regulation 1935/2004 on food-contact materials, providing a declaration of compliance for each article. Incoming inspection is performed at Vantera plants on an AQL 2.5 sampling basis for major defects and AQL 1.0 for critical defects. A non-conforming delivery is quarantined, a non-conformance report is raised within 2 business days, and Batavia responds with containment within 24 hours and a root cause analysis using the 8D methodology within 10 business days. Specification changes, substrate changes, and site transfers require prior written approval from Vantera Packaging Development, and any change affecting recyclability additionally requires Sustainable Procurement approval.

Service Levels

On-time in-full delivery is measured monthly against the confirmed delivery date, with a target of 98%. Lead time is 15 working days for standard articles and 25 working days for articles requiring new print origination. Batavia holds 4 weeks of safety stock of the top 20 articles by volume at its own cost, and reports stock levels weekly.

Tooling and Intellectual Property

Print cylinders, cutting dies, and origination artwork paid for by Vantera remain Vantera property, are recorded in the tooling register with asset identifiers, and must be returned or destroyed on instruction at the end of the agreement. Vantera artwork, brand assets, and structural designs remain Vantera intellectual property and may not be used for any other customer, including in modified form.

Sustainability Commitments

Batavia provides material composition and recycled content data per article, supports the Vantera commitment that all packaging is reusable, recyclable, or compostable, provides primary Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions data annually, and holds FSC chain of custody certification for fibre-based articles. Batavia's current EcoVadis score is 62, which satisfies the Silver requirement applicable to Tier 1 suppliers.

Liability and Termination

Liability is capped at 150% of the charges paid in the preceding 12 months, with the standard uncapped carve-outs, and product liability cover of €10,000,000 is maintained given the food-contact application. Vantera may terminate for convenience on 6 months' notice given the manufacturing lead times involved, for material breach not remedied within 30 days, and immediately on insolvency. On termination, Batavia sells and Vantera purchases finished goods and work in progress made to Vantera specification against firm forecast, and raw material purchased against the firm forecast window.

title: Cloud Services Agreement Summary — Meridian Cloud Services, Inc. (CSA-MER-2026-001)
text:
Parties and Structure

This is a summary of cloud services agreement CSA-MER-2026-001 between Vantera Group N.V. and Meridian Cloud Services, Inc., supplier identifier SUP-103010, incorporated in Delaware and contracting through its Irish subsidiary for European services. The agreement comprises the master cloud services agreement, the service description schedule, the service level schedule, the data processing addendum, and the commitment and pricing schedule. Meridian's online service terms are incorporated only as fixed at version 2026.1 as at 2026-02-01; unilateral changes by Meridian do not take effect without a written amendment.

Term and Financial Commitment

The initial term runs from 2026-02-01 to 2029-01-31. Vantera commits to a minimum spend of €3,000,000 per contract year in exchange for a 28% discount against Meridian's published list prices, with an additional 4% discount tier available above €4,500,000 of annual consumption. Unused commitment does not roll forward beyond the contract year in which it arises. Where actual consumption falls below the commitment, Vantera pays the shortfall, which is why consumption is reviewed quarterly by the FinOps forum against the commitment glide path.

Availability Service Level

Meridian commits to monthly availability of 99.9% for production compute, storage, and managed database services, measured per service and per region, excluding scheduled maintenance notified at least 7 days in advance and capped at 4 hours per calendar month. Availability is calculated as total minutes in the month less unavailable minutes, divided by total minutes, expressed as a percentage.

Service Credits

Service credits are calculated against the monthly charges for the affected service in the affected region.
Availability below 99.9% and at or above 99.0%: 5% credit.
Availability below 99.0% and at or above 95.0%: 10% credit.
Availability below 95.0%: 25% credit.
Credits must be claimed within 30 days of the end of the affected month, and Vantera's entitlement is not automatic, which is why the platform team files claims from monitoring data as part of the monthly service review. Service credits are capped at 30% of monthly charges for the affected service and are the exclusive remedy for availability failure, save that three consecutive months below 99.0%, or any single month below 95.0%, entitles Vantera to terminate the affected service without penalty and without loss of the commitment discount on remaining services.

Support and Incident Response

Support is provided on a 24 hours a day, 7 days a week basis for Severity 1 incidents with a 15-minute response target, Severity 2 with a 1-hour response target during business hours, and Severity 3 with a 1 business day response target. A named technical account manager is assigned, and a root cause analysis is provided within 5 business days for any Severity 1 incident.

Data Residency and Protection

All Vantera production data is stored and processed within the European Union, in the Dublin and Frankfurt regions, and Meridian may not relocate data outside the European Union without prior written approval. Support personnel outside the European Union may access data only through a documented break-glass process with Vantera approval per instance, logged and reviewed monthly. The data processing addendum incorporates Standard Contractual Clauses for any onward transfer, and Meridian maintains ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and ISO 27018 certifications, with evidence refreshed annually. Breach notification is required within 24 hours of Meridian becoming aware.

Security and Access Controls

Meridian provides customer-managed encryption keys for storage services, with Vantera retaining the ability to revoke access. Administrative access by Meridian personnel to Vantera tenancy requires just-in-time elevation with Vantera approval, and access logs are exportable to the Vantera security information and event management platform in near real time.

Price Protection and Renewal

List prices for the committed service catalogue may not increase during the initial term. New services added to the catalogue are available at the same discount tier. At renewal, any increase is capped at the euro area harmonised index of consumer prices plus 2 percentage points, and Meridian must give 120 days' notice of renewal pricing. The renewal decision point is 2027-11-01, which is 120 days before the notice deadline of 2028-11-02 under the 90-day notice provision.

Exit and Transition

On termination or expiry for any reason, Meridian provides transition assistance for up to 90 days at the rates in the pricing schedule, plus a 30-day data export window during which Vantera may extract all data at no egress charge. Data must be provided in documented, non-proprietary formats. Meridian must delete Vantera data within 60 days after the export window closes and certify deletion in writing. Meridian may not suspend services or withhold data because of a payment dispute, provided the disputed amount is being handled through the contractual dispute process and undisputed amounts are paid.

Liability and Governance

Liability is capped at 150% of charges paid in the preceding 12 months, with uncapped carve-outs for data protection breach, confidentiality breach, intellectual property infringement, fraud, and wilful misconduct. Cyber liability insurance of €10,000,000 is maintained, exceeding the €5,000,000 Tier-1 minimum. Governance comprises a monthly service review, a quarterly business review with the Technology Category Manager, and an annual architecture and roadmap session. The agreement is governed by Irish law with jurisdiction in Dublin.

title: Framework Agreement Summary — Orion Facility Services, S.A. (FA-ORI-2026-002)
text:
Parties and Scope

This is a summary of framework agreement FA-ORI-2026-002 between Vantera Iberia, S.L.U. and Orion Facility Services, S.A., supplier identifier SUP-102044, registered in Barcelona. Orion provides cleaning, waste management, grounds maintenance, reception, and pest control services at nine Vantera sites in Spain, comprising two manufacturing plants, two distribution centres, four offices, and one research facility. Site-specific scope, headcount, service frequencies, and standards are set out in individual site schedules, which are ordered against the framework and do not create separate agreements.

Term and Volume

The framework runs from 2026-03-01 to 2029-02-28, with no automatic renewal. Volumes are not guaranteed. Sites may be added or removed on 60 days' notice, with the rate card applying automatically to added sites of comparable type, and the removal of a site does not entitle Orion to compensation beyond demobilisation costs evidenced and agreed in advance.

Labour Standards and Living Wage

Because facilities services is a high-risk category under the responsible sourcing policy, this agreement contains enhanced labour provisions. Orion must comply with the applicable Spanish sectoral collective agreement for the cleaning industry in each province where services are performed, and must evidence compliance through payroll summaries provided quarterly. Orion commits that no worker assigned to a Vantera site is paid below the applicable living wage benchmark published by the Living Wage Foundation equivalent used in Spain, where that benchmark exceeds the collective agreement rate. Orion may not charge recruitment fees to workers, may not retain workers' identity documents, and must ensure that every worker receives a written contract in a language they understand before starting work.

Working Time and Wellbeing

Orion must ensure that assigned workers do not exceed the working time limits in Spanish law and the applicable collective agreement, including where a worker holds a second assignment with Orion at another client. Overtime must be voluntary and paid at the contractual premium. Orion reports monthly on assigned headcount, average hours worked, overtime hours, and turnover rate, and a turnover rate above 35% annually at any site triggers a joint review, because high turnover in this category is a reliable leading indicator of pay, workload, or management problems.

Subcontracting

Subcontracting requires Vantera's prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld for specialist services such as high-level window cleaning, pest control treatments, and confined space work. Subcontracting is limited to one tier below Orion; onward subcontracting by a subcontractor is prohibited. Orion remains fully responsible for the acts and omissions of subcontractors, must flow down the labour standards in this agreement in full, and must provide the subcontractor's name, registration number, and scope before mobilisation. Undisclosed subcontracting is a material breach.

Audit Rights

Vantera may conduct an announced social audit annually and an unannounced audit at any time where a concern is raised, including worker interviews conducted privately and without Orion management present. Orion must provide access to payroll records, working time records, contracts of employment, and subcontractor records for workers assigned to Vantera sites. The audit programme follows the SMETA four-pillar methodology through an independent audit body. Findings are classified as critical, major, or minor, with critical findings requiring containment within 24 hours and closure within 30 days.

Grievance Mechanism

Orion must inform assigned workers of the Vantera supply chain grievance mechanism, must display the contact details at each site in Spanish and in the principal languages spoken by the workforce, and must not retaliate against any worker who raises a concern. Vantera may participate directly in the remediation of substantiated grievances.

Service Levels and Quality

Performance is measured monthly on a site audit score with a target of 90%, response time to reactive requests of 4 hours for urgent and 2 business days for standard, complaint volume, and health and safety incident rate. Failure to achieve 90% for two consecutive months triggers a corrective action plan, and three consecutive months entitles Vantera to remove a site from the framework without demobilisation compensation.

Pricing and Indexation

Pricing is per site per month for the base scope, with an hourly rate card for additional and reactive work. Annual price review takes effect on 1 March each year and is limited to the pass-through of mandatory increases in the applicable collective agreement wage rates and statutory social security contributions, evidenced by the published agreement, plus a maximum 1% for other costs. Orion must not apply a general inflation uplift to the labour element in addition to the collective agreement pass-through.

Transfer of Undertakings and Termination

The parties acknowledge that Spanish transfer of undertakings rules may apply on entry and exit, and Orion must provide anonymised workforce data annually so that Vantera can inform a future bidder. Vantera may terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice, for material breach not remedied within 30 days, and immediately for a confirmed serious human rights breach that Orion fails to remediate. Insurance requirements are general liability of €5,000,000 and employer's liability at the statutory level.

title: Master Services Agreement Summary — Cobalt Talent Partners Ltd. (MSA-CTP-2025-011)
section_headings: Right to Work, Screening and Termination
text:
Parties and Model

This is a summary of master services agreement MSA-CTP-2025-011 between Vantera UK Ltd. and Cobalt Talent Partners Ltd., supplier identifier SUP-101876, registered in Manchester. Cobalt operates as the managed service provider for contingent labour across Vantera's United Kingdom and Ireland operations, managing a supply chain of approved recruitment agencies through a vendor management system. Cobalt supplies some workers directly and sources others through second-tier agencies, and in both cases Cobalt is the sole contractual counterparty to Vantera.

Term and Commercial Model

The agreement runs from 2025-09-01 to 2028-08-31. Cobalt charges a managed service fee of 8% of the worker pay rate for directly supplied workers and 2.5% of the agency charge rate for workers supplied through second-tier agencies. The fee is transparent and separately invoiced; margin may not be embedded in worker rates. Cobalt provides quarterly rate benchmarking against the market for each role family, and Vantera may require a rate card review where benchmark data shows a variance greater than 10%.

Rate Card and Approval

Rates are governed by the Schedule 2 rate card, structured by role family, skill grade, and location, with separate columns for the pay rate, employer costs, agency margin, and total charge rate. A request above the rate card requires approval from the HR Services Category Manager and the hiring director, and the business justification must state why the standard rate cannot attract the required skill. Rate exceptions are reviewed quarterly, and a role family with a persistent exception rate above 20% is a signal that the rate card is out of date rather than that hiring managers are being unreasonable.

Worker Classification and IR35

For every engagement, Vantera as the end client determines employment status for tax purposes and issues a status determination statement before the worker starts, with reasons. Cobalt operates the disagreement process and must not begin an assignment without a status determination statement in place. Where an engagement is determined to be inside the off-payroll working rules, the deemed employer obligations sit with the fee-payer in the chain, and Cobalt must confirm in writing which entity is the fee-payer for each assignment. Cobalt indemnifies Vantera against any tax, national insurance, interest, and penalties arising from Cobalt's failure to operate payroll correctly where it is the fee-payer, and from any misrepresentation of a worker's engagement model. Personal service company engagements require documented status determination and may not be used to re-engage a former employee within 6 months of leaving without HR approval.

Co-Employment Risk Controls

Contingent workers are not Vantera employees and must not be treated as such. Vantera managers must not conduct performance appraisals for contingent workers, must not include them in employee bonus, recognition, or benefit schemes, must not manage their leave or absence directly, and must not offer them a permanent role except through the agreed transfer process. Cobalt is responsible for holiday, sickness, disciplinary, and grievance matters relating to its workers.

Tenure Limits

No contingent worker may remain on assignment at Vantera for longer than 24 consecutive months. An extension beyond 24 months requires approval from the HR Director and the Category Director, and requires a documented plan to either convert the role to a permanent position or complete the work. A worker who has completed 24 months may not be re-engaged for the same or a substantially similar role within 6 months. This control exists to manage employment status risk, agency worker regulation entitlements, and the tendency for contingent resource to become a permanent structural cost invisible to headcount planning.

Agency Worker Regulations

After 12 weeks in the same role, agency workers become entitled to equal treatment on basic working and employment conditions. Cobalt is responsible for identifying qualifying workers, applying the entitlement, and adjusting the charge rate accordingly with 30 days' notice. Cobalt reports monthly on workers approaching the 12-week qualifying period and the 24-month tenure limit.

Timesheets, Invoicing and Payment

Timesheets are submitted weekly by the worker and approved by the Vantera hiring manager by the following Tuesday. Unapproved timesheets after 10 business days are escalated to the hiring manager's director, because unapproved time is the leading cause of disputed invoices in this category. Cobalt self-bills weekly from approved timesheets, and payment terms are Net 30, which is shorter than the Vantera standard because the majority of the charge is worker pay.

Right to Work, Screening and Termination

Cobalt verifies right to work, references, and any role-specific screening such as a criminal records check for roles with site access, before an assignment starts, and retains evidence for the duration plus 12 months. Assignments may be terminated by Vantera on 5 business days' notice without cost beyond time worked. The agreement may be terminated for convenience on 90 days' notice, and immediately for a serious breach including a failure of right to work checks.

title: RFP Scoring and Award Guide — Logistics and Transport Categories
text:
Purpose

This guide explains how to build and run an evaluation model for logistics and transport sourcing events. It applies to road, rail, sea, and air freight, to warehousing and contract logistics, to parcel and last mile, and to temperature-controlled transport. It is guidance rather than policy, but the weighting limits and the process requirements it references are mandatory under the Competitive Sourcing and Bidding Policy.

Recommended Evaluation Criteria

A logistics evaluation model should score providers across six dimensions: price and total cost of ownership, service coverage and network fit, service level performance and operational capability, carbon reporting and environmental performance, claims handling and quality management, and implementation approach and timeline. Additional dimensions such as technology and visibility, financial stability, and labour standards should be added where they materially differentiate.

Weighting Guidance

Price should not exceed 40% of the total score in logistics categories, and for temperature-controlled and pharmaceutical-grade transport it should not exceed 30%. This is not a preference for expensive suppliers; it reflects the fact that in transport the cheapest bid frequently becomes the most expensive contract once failed deliveries, re-deliveries, claims, and emergency backup transport are included. A workable default for a general road distribution event is price 40%, service level and operational capability 20%, network coverage and fit 15%, implementation 10%, carbon and environmental 10%, and claims and quality 5%. Weightings must be fixed and approved before bids are opened, and may not be adjusted afterwards.

Building the Price Comparison

Never compare headline rates. Build a total cost of ownership model that applies each bidder's rate card to a fixed, published lane and volume profile taken from the previous 12 months of actual shipments, so that every bidder is priced on identical demand. The model must include base linehaul rates by lane, fuel surcharge mechanism and its baseline, accessorial charges including waiting time, re-delivery, failed delivery, out-of-hours, pallet exchange, and returns, minimum charges and rounding rules, implementation and onboarding costs, and the working capital effect of the payment terms offered. Ask bidders to price the accessorials explicitly, because a low linehaul rate combined with aggressive accessorial charging is a common bidding strategy and is invisible in a rate-card comparison.

Fuel Surcharge Mechanisms

Compare the mechanism, not the current value. A fuel surcharge must specify the published index used, the baseline index value and date, the fuel-attributable percentage of the rate, the review frequency, the deadband, and the lag between index movement and rate change. A bidder offering a low base rate with an aggressive fuel mechanism, for example no deadband and a high fuel-attributable percentage, will normally be more expensive within a year. Ask every bidder to price the same historical index series through their proposed mechanism, which converts an opaque clause into a comparable number.

Evaluating Service Capability

Score demonstrated performance, not stated capability. Request lane-level on-time delivery performance for comparable customers over the previous 12 months, the measurement definition used, and the source system. A bidder quoting a 99% on-time figure measured at depot departure is not comparable to one quoting 97% measured at delivery point within the customer window. Request network maps, depot locations and ownership, subcontracting percentage by lane, driver employment model, and fleet age and composition. A high subcontracting percentage is not disqualifying but changes the risk profile and should be reflected in the operational scoring and in the contract.

Temperature-Controlled Requirements

For temperature-controlled transport, audit evidence and lane-level service history must be reviewed before award, and this review is a gate rather than a scored item. Required evidence includes temperature mapping validation for each vehicle type, calibration certificates for temperature recording equipment with the calibration interval, continuous monitoring capability with alerting and the data retention period, documented procedures for a temperature excursion including notification timing to the customer, HACCP or equivalent food safety certification, and evidence of the last regulatory or customer audit with findings and closure status. A bidder that cannot produce excursion records is not demonstrating a perfect record; it is demonstrating that it does not measure.

Carbon and Environmental Scoring

Score the ability to report primary data, not aspiration. Ask for CO2 per pallet-kilometre or per shipment calculated to a stated methodology such as GLEC or EN 16258, the proportion of the fleet meeting the current emission standard, low-emission vehicle deployment plans with dates, load fill and empty running rates, and whether the bidder can provide shipment-level emissions data into Vantera's reporting. A bidder that can only provide a fleet-average figure cannot support Scope 3 reporting at the granularity Vantera needs.

Running the Evaluation

Score independently before the consensus meeting, so that panel members are not anchored by the first opinion voiced. Record the rationale for each score, not merely the number, because the rationale is what makes an award defensible six months later. Where a bidder is excluded at a gate, record the gate and the evidence. Debrief unsuccessful bidders within 10 business days, focusing on their proposal's strengths and weaknesses without disclosing competitor information; a well-run debrief materially improves the quality of that bidder's next proposal.

Common Failure Modes

The recurring errors in this category are scoring a promise rather than evidence, comparing rates rather than total cost, allowing a single stakeholder's incumbent preference to dominate consensus scoring, underestimating implementation effort for a depot or system change, and awarding on a rate card that lacks a volume commitment, which permits the supplier to reprice the moment the profile shifts.

title: Category Playbook — Software, SaaS and Cloud Procurement
section_headings: Security, Data Protection and AI Terms
Working with Enterprise Architecture and InfoSec
text:
Purpose

This playbook sets out how Vantera buys software, software as a service, and cloud infrastructure. The category is characterised by high renewal leverage held by the supplier, opaque licence metrics, and a persistent tendency for committed spend to exceed consumed value.

Start Twelve Months Before Renewal

The single highest-value action in this category is starting early. At 12 months before renewal, pull actual usage data: licences assigned versus licences consumed in the last 90 days, feature usage by module, consumption against any committed spend, and the number of users who have not logged in for 60 days. At 9 months, establish whether the requirement still exists in its current form and whether a credible alternative exists, including doing nothing, consolidating into an existing platform, or reducing scope. At 6 months, open the commercial conversation with a clear position. A renewal opened 30 days before expiry has no leverage, and every supplier account team knows exactly how much time is left.

Licence Metrics and Their Traps

Understand precisely what the metric counts before negotiating price. Named user licences are counted whether or not the user is active, so unassigned or dormant licences are pure cost. Concurrent user licences count peak simultaneous use and require monitoring evidence to size correctly. Consumption metrics such as API calls, records, documents, or compute units grow with business activity rather than with headcount, and must be modelled against a growth forecast before committing. Processor and core-based metrics for on-premises software interact with virtualisation policies in ways that create audit exposure. Ask for the definition in writing, ask how it is measured, and ask who measures it.

Commitment Discounts

Suppliers offer discounts for multi-year and multi-volume commitments. Commitment is only worth taking where the requirement is genuinely stable, the discount is material, and unused commitment does not simply evaporate. Negotiate for unused commitment to roll forward within the term, for the ability to reallocate commitment across services or business units, and for a right to reduce the committed volume by an agreed percentage at each anniversary. A three-year commitment at a 30% discount that is 40% unconsumed in year two is more expensive than list price.

Price Protection and Uplift Caps

Every agreement should cap renewal uplift. The Vantera standard is a cap at the euro area harmonised index of consumer prices plus 2 percentage points, applied to the renewal of the same scope. Without a cap, the standard supplier model is a mid to high single-digit annual uplift compounding across the relationship. Also fix the discount percentage rather than the absolute price, so that the discount survives a list price increase, and secure the same discount tier for services added later.

True-Up and Audit Provisions

Negotiate the audit clause before it matters. Limit audits to once per 12 months on at least 30 days' notice, restrict them to the relevant licence data rather than open access to systems, require the auditor to sign confidentiality terms, and require any shortfall to be settled at the contracted discount rather than at list price. Require the supplier to provide the tooling or reporting needed for Vantera to self-assess compliance, since a supplier that will not tell you how it counts is reserving the right to count in its favour.

Security, Data Protection and AI Terms

Security assessment starts at shortlist, not after award, and the requirements in the information security policy apply regardless of contract value. For any supplier offering artificial intelligence features, establish in writing whether Vantera data, prompts, uploaded documents, or outputs are used for model training or evaluation, whether they are retained and for how long, whether human review occurs, which sub-processors and model providers are involved, and whether the feature can be disabled at tenant level. The prohibition on model training without written approval must appear as an express contractual term rather than as a reference to a supplier policy page that the supplier can change.

Exit Planning at Entry

Negotiate exit terms while you still have leverage, which is before signature. Require data export in documented, non-proprietary formats, a defined transition assistance period, no egress charges during an agreed export window, deletion certification, and an express prohibition on withholding data during a commercial dispute. For platforms holding transactional history, establish what the export actually contains, because an export that omits attachments, audit history, or configuration is not a usable exit.

Consolidation and Demand Management

The largest savings in this category usually come from removing duplication rather than from negotiating a better rate. Maintain an application inventory with owner, renewal date, cost, user count, and business capability. Where two platforms serve the same capability, the category strategy should force a decision. Reclaim dormant licences quarterly through an automated report to line managers, and make licence cost visible at cost centre level, because invisible cost is never optimised.

Working with Enterprise Architecture and InfoSec

Every software requisition routes automatically to Enterprise Architecture and InfoSec Procurement. Engage both before shortlisting rather than at approval, because a late architectural objection or a failed security assessment after commercial agreement wastes the negotiation and damages credibility with the supplier.

title: Negotiation Guide — Cost Models, Price Indexation and Should-Cost Analysis for Direct Materials
text:
Purpose

This guide explains how to build a cost model, how to structure a price indexation mechanism, and how to negotiate direct material prices on evidence rather than on percentage demands. It applies to packaging, ingredients, and other bought-in materials where the price is materially driven by a traded or published input.

Why Indexation Beats Annual Negotiation

An annual price negotiation on a material whose cost is driven by a public index is a negotiation about information asymmetry rather than about value. Indexation replaces it with a rule agreed once: when the index moves, the price moves by a defined, calculable amount. The benefits are that price changes become predictable and auditable, that negotiation effort shifts to the elements that are genuinely negotiable, being conversion cost, waste, yield, and margin, and that the supplier is neither punished nor rewarded for input movements outside its control.

Building a Should-Cost Model

A should-cost model estimates what a part ought to cost from first principles. Build it bottom up: raw material input weight including yield loss and scrap rate, at a published market price; conversion cost derived from machine cycle time, line rate, and an hourly machine rate that includes labour, energy, depreciation, and overhead absorption; tooling amortisation over the expected volume; quality, testing, and packaging costs; inbound and outbound logistics on the agreed Incoterm; and a reasonable margin for the industry and the risk carried. The model does not need to be exactly right to be valuable. Its purpose is to make the conversation specific, so that instead of arguing about a 6% increase you are discussing whether the yield loss assumption is 4% or 7%.

Anatomy of an Indexation Clause

A workable indexation clause specifies each of the following, and ambiguity in any one of them is where disputes originate. The index must be named precisely, including the publisher, series name, geography, grade, and the exact publication used, because index families contain many similar series. The material component must be fixed as a percentage of the price, so that indexation applies only to the input it relates to; if the whole price is indexed to a resin price, the supplier's labour and margin are being indexed to resin. The baseline must state the index value and the date it corresponds to, since a mechanism without a baseline cannot be recalculated. The review frequency should be quarterly for most materials and monthly only for highly volatile inputs, because more frequent reviews create administrative cost and price instability. The deadband, typically 2% to 3%, prevents small movements from triggering changes, and the clause must state whether movements inside the deadband are ignored or carried forward to the next review. The lag and notice period should be at least 30 to 60 days so that plans and customer prices can be adjusted. A cap and collar should be considered where extreme volatility would be unmanageable for either party.

Symmetry and Verification

Indexation must operate in both directions and with the same mechanics. The most common failure in practice is not a badly drafted clause but an unenforced one: suppliers reliably submit increases when the index rises, and reductions are frequently missed when it falls. Assign a named owner to recalculate every indexed article each review cycle from the published index, independently of the supplier's submission. Require the supplier to provide the index value, the calculation, and the resulting price with each change, and hold open-book audit rights over the calculation. Where a supplier claims an increase greater than the mechanism produces, treat it as a commercial renegotiation subject to normal approval, not as an index adjustment.

Negotiating the Non-Indexed Elements

Conversion, waste, and margin are where genuine negotiation lives. Useful levers include specification simplification such as reducing substrate weight, colour count, or tolerance where the technical function permits, run length and changeover reduction achieved by consolidating articles, yield improvement through joint work on scrap rates, packaging and pallet configuration to improve transport fill, payment terms and their working capital value, and volume consolidation across plants where a supplier's footprint permits. Each of these produces a cost change that can be evidenced, which is what makes the saving durable.

Hedging and Forward Buying

Where a material has a liquid forward market, consider whether to fix a price forward. This is a Treasury decision as much as a procurement one, and the position must be agreed with Treasury and Finance, because fixing forward is a market view, not a saving. Document the reference price at the time of fixing so that the outcome can be evaluated honestly afterwards rather than reinterpreted.

Governance

Indexation mechanisms and cost models are reviewed by the Category Council annually, and any change to a mechanism requires a contract amendment. Savings claimed from indexation mechanics are reported separately from negotiated savings, because reporting a price reduction that the index produced automatically as a negotiated saving misrepresents performance and erodes the credibility of the whole savings figure.

title: Incoterms 2020 Selection Guide for Inbound Logistics
text:
Purpose

This guide explains which Incoterms 2020 rules Vantera uses for inbound purchases, why the choice matters commercially and not only operationally, and which rules to avoid. Incoterms allocate three things between buyer and seller: who arranges and pays for transport, where risk of loss passes, and who handles export and import customs formalities. They do not determine ownership, payment terms, or the transfer of title.

Preferred Rules for Inbound Purchases

FCA, being Free Carrier at a named place, is the preferred rule for international purchases where Vantera controls the freight. The seller delivers goods, cleared for export, to a carrier nominated by Vantera at a named place, and risk passes at that point. FCA is preferred over EXW because the seller handles export clearance, which the seller is legally and practically better placed to do, and because under EXW the buyer is formally responsible for an export declaration in a country where it may have no legal presence.
DAP, being Delivered at Place, is the preferred rule for intra-European road purchases where the supplier's transport is efficient or where consolidated deliveries are involved. The seller bears cost and risk to the named destination, and Vantera handles import clearance and pays import duties and taxes where applicable.
CIP, being Carriage and Insurance Paid To, is used where insurance cover through to destination is required and the seller arranges transport. Under Incoterms 2020, CIP requires the seller to obtain insurance at Institute Cargo Clauses A level, which is all-risks cover, a change from the 2010 edition where the lower Clauses C level applied.

Rules to Avoid and Why

EXW should be avoided for international movements. The buyer takes risk from the seller's premises, including during loading, and takes formal responsibility for export clearance in the seller's country. Where a supplier insists on EXW, negotiate FCA at the seller's premises instead, which achieves a similar commercial position while placing export clearance where it belongs.
DDP should be avoided in most cases. The seller bears all costs including import duties and taxes, which appears convenient but means Vantera loses visibility of the duty paid, cannot reclaim import VAT where it is not the importer of record, cannot apply preferential origin claims it may be entitled to, and is exposed if the supplier's customs declarations are incorrect while Vantera is the beneficial owner of the goods.
Sea-only rules FAS, FOB, CFR, and CIF should be used only for bulk and break-bulk cargo actually loaded on board a vessel. They are frequently and incorrectly applied to containerised shipments, where the goods are handed over at a terminal rather than loaded over the ship's rail, which creates a gap between where risk formally passes and where the goods actually leave the seller's control.

Total Cost Implications

An Incoterm is a pricing term as much as a logistics term, and bids using different Incoterms are not comparable until normalised. When comparing bids, restate every offer on a single agreed basis, adding or removing freight, insurance, terminal handling, export and import clearance, duty, and inland transport as required. A supplier offering DAP at a price 4% above an FCA competitor may be materially cheaper once freight is included, or materially more expensive if it is embedding a margin on freight that Vantera could buy directly at a contracted rate.

Named Place Precision

Always state the named place precisely and identically in the contract, the purchase order, and the transport instructions. FCA Rotterdam is ambiguous; FCA Batavia Packaging B.V. warehouse, Waalhaven, Rotterdam, Incoterms 2020 is not. Ambiguity in the named place is the single most common source of dispute about who pays for loading, waiting time, and terminal handling charges.

Insurance and Claims

Under FCA and DAP, confirm which party's cargo insurance responds and ensure there is no gap at the point of risk transfer. Vantera maintains an open cargo policy for goods purchased on terms where Vantera bears transit risk, and buyers must notify Global Trade and Logistics when a new lane or a high-value movement begins so that cover is confirmed. Claims must be notified promptly, and delivery notes must be annotated at the point of delivery where damage or shortage is apparent, since an unqualified clean receipt materially weakens a later claim.

Customs, Origin and Documentation

Confirm at sourcing whether preferential origin can be claimed under an applicable trade agreement, and require the supplier to provide a valid origin declaration or statement on origin, since the duty saving is often larger than the negotiated price difference between bidders. Ensure commodity codes are agreed and consistent, and that commercial invoices contain the data customs requires. Errors here create retrospective duty demands and penalties that arrive long after the buyer has moved on to another category.

Recording the Agreed Term

The agreed Incoterm, edition year, and named place must be recorded in the contract, the article master, and on every purchase order. Purchase orders that omit the Incoterm default to the contract term, and where no contract exists the order is raised only after the term is agreed in writing.

title: Contingent Labour and Professional Services Sourcing Guide
section_headings: Writing a Usable Statement of Work
text:
Purpose

This guide explains how to buy contingent labour and professional services, how to decide between a time-and-materials engagement and a deliverable-based statement of work, and how to write a statement of work that can be managed and receipted objectively.

Choosing the Engagement Model

The first decision is whether Vantera is buying capacity or buying an outcome. Buy capacity, through a contingent worker on a time-and-materials basis, where Vantera knows what needs doing and how, directs the work day to day, and needs an additional pair of hands with a specific skill. Buy an outcome, through a deliverable-based statement of work, where the supplier brings a method, carries delivery risk, and can be held to a defined result. The failure mode to avoid is a consultancy engagement priced by the day with no defined deliverable, which is capacity purchased at outcome prices, and which cannot be assessed for value at the end.

Rate Cards and Benchmarking

Contingent rates are governed by the managed service provider rate card, structured by role family, skill grade, and location, showing the pay rate, employer costs, agency margin, and total charge rate separately. Transparency matters because the negotiable element is the margin, not the pay rate; pushing the pay rate down usually reduces candidate quality and increases turnover, while margin is a genuine commercial variable. Benchmark rate cards at least annually, and treat a persistent rate exception rate above 20% in a role family as evidence the rate card is stale.

Writing a Usable Statement of Work

A statement of work must contain a background and objective explaining why the work is being done, a specific scope with explicit exclusions, a list of deliverables each with acceptance criteria that a third party could apply, a milestone schedule with dates, the payment schedule linked to milestone acceptance rather than to elapsed time, the named key personnel with a right of approval over replacements, Vantera's dependencies and the consequence if they are late, assumptions with the mechanism for handling a change of assumption, the change control process, and intellectual property and data protection terms. Acceptance criteria are the element most often omitted and most often needed. A deliverable described as a strategy document is not acceptable or rejectable; a deliverable described as a strategy document covering the four defined workstreams, presented to the steering group, and including a costed implementation roadmap, is.

Milestone Payments and Retention

Link payment to accepted deliverables. A common structure is 20% on mobilisation, 60% across defined milestones, and 20% on final acceptance, with the final tranche retained until the acceptance criteria are met. Avoid paying more than 30% before any deliverable is accepted. Where a supplier requires higher upfront payment, treat it as a signal about the supplier's own cash position and consider it in the risk assessment.

Approval and Routing

Contingent labour requisitions route automatically to Human Resources in addition to the standard approval band under the Global Procurement Policy, and consultancy engagements above €250,000 require a formal request for proposal. Extensions require the same approval as the original engagement based on the cumulative value, not the incremental value, since the total committed value governs the approval band.

Co-Employment and Status Risk

Contingent workers are not employees and must not be managed as employees. Vantera managers must not conduct appraisals, must not include contingent workers in employee schemes, must not manage leave directly, and must route conduct or performance concerns through the managed service provider. In the United Kingdom, an employment status determination statement must be issued before the assignment starts. Across the European Union, the applicable rules on temporary agency work and on false self-employment differ by country, and the local Human Resources team must confirm the position before an engagement model is chosen. The commercial consequence of getting this wrong, being back taxes, social contributions, penalties, and potential employment claims, is typically far larger than the rate saving that motivated the arrangement.

Tenure and Structural Drift

Apply the 24-month tenure limit consistently, and review long-running engagements annually against the question of whether the work is genuinely temporary. Contingent resource that has been in place for years is usually a permanent role being funded outside headcount, which distorts workforce planning and typically costs 20% to 40% more than the equivalent employee.

Knowledge Transfer and Exit

Require a knowledge transfer plan and documentation as an explicit deliverable in any engagement of more than three months, and make final payment conditional on it. Confirm at the outset that work product, including code, models, documents, and data, is Vantera intellectual property, and that the supplier will return or delete Vantera data at the end of the engagement.

Measuring Value

At the end of an engagement, record whether the deliverables were accepted on time, whether the outcome was achieved, and whether the supplier would be used again for similar work. This record is the only reliable input to the next sourcing decision in a category where reputation and relationship frequently substitute for evidence.

title: Supplier Performance Scorecard Q2 2026 — Acme Logistics S.L.
text:
Scorecard Summary

This is the Q2 2026 performance scorecard for Acme Logistics S.L., supplier identifier SUP-100482, covering the period 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30 under master services agreement MSA-ACM-2024-018. Acme is segmented as a Tier 1 strategic supplier with annual spend of €4,200,000. The overall score for the quarter is 82 out of 100, which is a pass under the supplier performance procedure, down from 87 in Q1 2026.

Dimension Scores

Quality (26 of 30): damage rate improved to 0.18% of delivered cases against a target of 0.20%, and there were 4 non-conformance reports in the quarter, all closed within the agreed timescale. One repeat issue on pallet quality at the Valencia depot remains open as an improvement action.
Delivery (19 of 25): on-time delivery averaged 98.2% against the contractual service level of 98.5%, with the shortfall concentrated in April and May. Order fill rate was 99.3% against a 99.2% target. Electronic proof of delivery transmission within 4 hours was achieved on 98.4% of deliveries against a 99% target.
Cost (17 of 20): the agreed cost reduction of €95,000 against the annual baseline was delivered. Two fuel surcharge calculations were submitted without the supporting index reference and were returned, and invoice first-time-right was 93.1%.
Service and responsiveness (12 of 15): stakeholder survey scores were solid on day-to-day responsiveness and weaker on proactive communication during the May disruption. Claims acknowledgement met the 2 business day requirement in all cases; claims resolution averaged 17 business days against the 20 business day target.
Sustainability and compliance (8 of 10): EcoVadis score of 58 is above the €250,000 spend threshold minimum of 45 but below the Silver level of 59 required for Tier 1 suppliers by 2027-01-01. CO2 per pallet delivered improved 3.1% year on year. Low-emission fleet conversion stands at 18% against the 30% commitment for 2027-12-31.

Monthly On-Time Delivery Detail

April 2026: 97.9% — below the 98.5% service level. Root cause was a driver shortage at the Guadalajara depot following an unplanned resignation cluster, compounded by the Easter delivery profile.
May 2026: 98.1% — below the 98.5% service level, the second consecutive missed measurement period. Root cause was a three-day regional industrial action affecting road access in Catalonia, for which Acme's force majeure claim was reviewed and rejected because the contract requires demonstration that the event prevented performance rather than made it more difficult, and other providers maintained service on the affected lanes.
June 2026: 98.7% — above the service level, which reset the consecutive-miss counter.

Service Credit Position

Because on-time delivery was missed in two consecutive monthly measurement periods, April and May 2026, a service credit became payable in respect of May 2026 under the service credit provisions of MSA-ACM-2024-018. The credit applied is 2% of May monthly charges, being €7,140, and was applied as a credit note against invoice INV-ACM-2026-0331. No further escalation of the credit percentage applied because June performance was compliant and the counter reset. The Category Manager confirmed that the credit was applied rather than waived, in line with the requirement that contractual credits be enforced consistently.

Open Actions

Action 1: Acme to submit a driver retention and resourcing plan for the Guadalajara depot, owner Acme operations director, due 2026-08-15. Status: submitted 2026-08-11, under review.
Action 2: Acme to include the index reference and calculation with every fuel surcharge submission, owner Acme commercial manager, due immediately. Status: closed 2026-07-01.
Action 3: Acme to present a plan to reach EcoVadis Silver before 2027-01-01, owner Acme sustainability lead, due 2026-09-30. Status: open.
Action 4: Joint review of the Valencia pallet quality issue with the Vantera site team, owner Iberia logistics manager, due 2026-08-31. Status: open.
Action 5: Vantera to improve delivery window forecast accuracy for promotional volumes, owner Vantera demand planning, due 2026-09-15. Status: open. This action was raised by Acme and accepted, since forecast volatility on promotional lines contributed to the April shortfall.

Vantera Performance Toward Acme

On-time payment against contractual terms was 96.4% in the quarter, below the 98% internal commitment. Three invoices were blocked for more than 20 business days on price variances traced to a fuel surcharge that had been agreed commercially but not updated on the open purchase orders. This was raised by Acme in the June quarterly business review and is accepted as a Vantera action.

Next Review

The Q3 2026 scorecard will be produced by 2026-10-15 and reviewed in the quarterly business review scheduled for 2026-10-22. The contract renewal decision point under the contract renewal procedure falls at 120 days before the notice deadline of 2027-02-11, and this scorecard forms part of the evidence base for that decision.
