section_headings: Finding 1 — Sole-Source Justifications Not Supported by Evidence (High)
Finding 2 — Requisition Splitting Below Approval Thresholds (High)
Finding 3 — Retrospective Purchase Orders Raised to Clear Invoices (Medium)
Finding 5 — Gifts and Hospitality Register Completeness (Medium)
text:
Scope and Objective

Group Internal Audit reviewed procure-to-pay controls at Vantera Iberia, S.L.U. between 2026-05-04 and 2026-06-26, covering the period 2025-07-01 to 2026-03-31. The objective was to assess whether spend approval, competitive sourcing, supplier onboarding, invoice processing, and purchase order controls operated effectively. Testing covered a sample of 120 purchase orders, 80 invoices, 25 sourcing events, 15 new supplier onboardings, and all 41 sourcing exceptions approved in the period. The overall opinion is Partially Effective, meaning that controls are designed adequately but operating effectiveness gaps exist that require management attention.

Finding 1 — Sole-Source Justifications Not Supported by Evidence (High)

Of the 41 sourcing exceptions approved in the period, 23 relied on the sole-source ground. Testing found that 9 of those 23 contained no evidence supporting the sole-source position beyond an assertion by the requester, such as a statement that the supplier is the only one capable of delivering to our standard. The competitive sourcing procedure requires evidence such as a patent reference, an exclusive distribution letter, a proprietary interface, or a regulatory approval. Aggregate value of the affected awards was €1,870,000. Root cause is that the exception form accepts free text without a mandatory evidence attachment, and approvers reported that they rely on the requester's assessment.
Management response: Procurement Governance will make evidence attachment mandatory in the Ariba Sourcing exception form and will introduce a pre-approval review by Procurement Governance for all sole-source exceptions above €100,000. Owner: Head of Procurement Governance. Due: 2026-11-30. Accepted.

Finding 2 — Requisition Splitting Below Approval Thresholds (High)

Analytical testing identified 14 instances where two or more requisitions were raised to the same supplier for the same scope within a rolling 90-day period, where the combined value would have required a higher approval band. In 6 instances the pattern was consistent with deliberate splitting, including three cases of requisitions of €4,800 and €4,900 raised to the same consultancy in the same month, each falling just below the €5,000 Category Manager threshold. Total value of the 14 instances was €412,000.
Management response: A monthly detective control will be implemented reporting same-supplier same-scope requisitions within 90 days, reviewed by Procurement Operations, with confirmed cases reported to Internal Audit as control breaches. Owner: Head of Procurement Operations. Due: 2026-10-31. Accepted.

Finding 3 — Retrospective Purchase Orders Raised to Clear Invoices (Medium)

Of 80 invoices tested, 11 were paid against a purchase order raised after the invoice was received. In 7 of these the retrospective flag was not used and no emergency justification was recorded, meaning the commitment was not visible as an unauthorised commitment and did not receive the required approval one band above the ordinary band. Two cases involved purchase orders raised on the same day the invoice was posted, with the goods receipt entered by the same user who raised the requisition.
Management response: The retrospective flag will be enforced by system validation where the purchase order creation date is later than the invoice receipt date, and the segregation of duties rule preventing the requisitioner from posting the goods receipt will be enforced as a hard block rather than a warning. Owner: Head of Procure-to-Pay. Due: 2026-12-15. Accepted.

Finding 4 — Blocked Invoice Ageing (Medium)

At 2026-03-31, 214 invoices with a value of €2,340,000 were blocked, of which 63 had been blocked for more than 20 business days and 18 for more than 90 days. The procedure requires escalation to the Category Director at 20 business days; no evidence of escalation was found for 49 of the 63 cases. The ageing creates both an unrecorded liability risk and a supplier relationship risk, and three suppliers had raised formal escalations about non-payment during the period.
Management response: Automated escalation will replace manual escalation, and blocked invoice ageing will become a standing item in the monthly business unit performance review. Owner: Procure-to-Pay Iberia lead. Due: 2026-09-30. Accepted.

Finding 5 — Gifts and Hospitality Register Completeness (Medium)

Interviews and expense record analysis identified 4 instances of supplier-funded hospitality above the €100 declaration threshold that were not recorded in the Gifts and Hospitality Register, including one instance involving a member of an active evaluation panel during a live sourcing event, which is prohibited outright. No evidence was found that the award outcome was affected, but the control failure is material given the anti-bribery exposure.
Management response: Targeted refresher training for the Iberia procurement and category teams, and a quarterly reconciliation between expense records and the register. Owner: Group Compliance with Iberia Procurement. Due: 2026-10-15. Accepted.

Finding 6 — Contract Metadata Completeness (Low)

Of 25 contracts sampled in Ariba Contracts, 6 had no expiry date recorded and 9 had no notice period recorded, meaning renewal alerts could not fire. One agreement had auto-renewed in January 2026 without a renewal decision being taken.
Management response: A data cleanse of the Iberia contract population will be completed, and contract creation will require expiry date and notice period as mandatory fields. Owner: Contract Management Office. Due: 2026-11-30. Accepted.

What Worked Well

Supplier onboarding controls tested effectively, with all 15 sampled onboardings containing complete sanctions screening, tax validation, and bank verification evidence, including documented callback verification. No exceptions were identified in payment run authorisation or in duplicate payment controls.

Follow-Up

Internal Audit will validate remediation of the two High findings in Q1 2027 and will report status to the Audit Committee quarterly until closure.

title: RFP Packet Summary — Temperature-Controlled Transport EMEA (RFP-EMEA-2026-0141)
text:
Event Overview

RFP-EMEA-2026-0141 is a formal request for proposal for temperature-controlled road transport across EMEA, launched on 2026-08-03 through Ariba Sourcing. Estimated annual addressable spend is €8,600,000 across chilled and frozen lanes serving Spain, Portugal, France, Germany, the Netherlands, and Poland. The intended contract structure is a three-year framework with two optional one-year extensions, awarded to a primary provider per region with a nominated backup provider for business-critical lanes. Because total committed value exceeds €1,000,000, a category strategy was approved by the Category Council on 2026-06-18 before launch, in line with the Competitive Sourcing and Bidding Policy.

Timeline

Category strategy approved: 2026-06-18.
Request for information issued to the long list of 14 providers: 2026-07-06.
Long list qualified to a short list of 6: 2026-07-28.
Request for proposal issued: 2026-08-03.
Bidder clarification window closes: 2026-08-21.
Site visits and cold chain capability audits: 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-18.
Proposals due: 2026-09-25 at 17:00 CET through Ariba Sourcing.
Evaluation and consensus scoring: 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-09.
Best and final offer round: 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-23.
Award recommendation to VP Procurement and CPO: 2026-11-06.
Contract signature target: 2026-12-15. Operational go-live: 2027-02-01.

Shortlisted Bidders

The six shortlisted providers are Helvetia Cold Chain AG (SUP-101233), Acme Logistics S.L. (SUP-100482) bidding for the Iberian lanes only, and four providers not currently in the Vantera supplier master who will complete onboarding due diligence before award rather than before bidding.

Mandatory Gate Criteria

The following are pass or fail gates assessed before scoring, and a bidder failing any gate is excluded regardless of commercial offer. Valid HACCP certification or an accepted equivalent food safety certification covering the transport operation. Temperature mapping validation for each vehicle type proposed, with reports no older than 24 months. Calibration certificates for temperature recording equipment, with a stated calibration interval no longer than 12 months. Continuous temperature monitoring with automated excursion alerting, and a data retention period of at least 24 months. A documented temperature excursion procedure specifying customer notification within 2 hours of detection. Twelve months of lane-level on-time delivery and excursion history for comparable customers, with the measurement definition stated. Evidence of the most recent regulatory or customer audit including findings and closure status. Insurance meeting the Vantera minimums, being general liability of €5,000,000 and goods-in-transit cover appropriate to the cargo value.

Evaluation Model

Weightings were fixed and approved before the request for proposal was issued and may not be changed after bid opening.
Price and total cost of ownership: 30%. Capped at 30% rather than 40% because this is temperature-controlled transport, where the cost of a failure materially exceeds the rate difference between bidders.
Operational capability and service level performance: 25%.
Cold chain integrity, monitoring and quality systems: 20%.
Network coverage, capacity and backup arrangements: 10%.
Carbon reporting and environmental performance: 10%.
Implementation approach and transition plan: 5%.

Price Comparison Basis

Bidders price a fixed lane and volume profile derived from the 12 months to 2026-06-30, comprising 41,200 chilled pallet movements and 18,700 frozen pallet movements across 63 defined lanes. The total cost model includes linehaul by lane, the fuel surcharge mechanism priced through the actual gasoil index series for the 24 months to 2026-06-30, accessorials including waiting time, re-delivery, failed delivery and temperature re-conditioning, minimum charges and rounding rules, implementation cost, and the working capital value of the payment terms offered. Bidders offering payment terms shorter than Net 60 are normalised in the model rather than advantaged.

Evaluation Panel

The panel comprises the EMEA Logistics Category Manager as chair, the Iberia logistics operations manager, the supply chain quality manager, a demand planning representative, and a Group Sustainability representative for the environmental criterion only. All panel members completed conflict of interest declarations before receiving bid documents. One panel member declared a former employment relationship with a shortlisted bidder that ended in 2021; Procurement Governance assessed the declaration and permitted participation with the mitigation that the member does not score the commercial criteria for that bidder.

Bidder Communication Rules

All clarification questions are submitted through Ariba Sourcing and are answered to all bidders simultaneously in anonymised form. No pricing information is shared between bidders in any form. The best and final offer round will be offered to all bidders remaining after consensus scoring on identical terms. Under the anti-bribery policy, no panel member may accept hospitality of any value from a participating bidder between launch and award communication, and this includes catering during site visits beyond ordinary working refreshments.

Award and Debrief

The award recommendation will document the evaluation outcome, the negotiated position against the baseline, the risk assessment result, and the recommended primary and backup providers by region. Unsuccessful bidders will be debriefed within 10 business days of award.

title: Category Council Decision Memo — Packaging Resin Indexation Review 2026
section_headings: Issue 1 — Asymmetric Application of the Mechanism
text:
Purpose of This Memo

This memo records the decisions taken by the Category Council on 2026-06-25 regarding the price indexation mechanism in supply agreement SA-BAT-2025-007 with Batavia Packaging B.V., supplier identifier SUP-100311, and the treatment of indexation movements in savings reporting. It is issued for the record and is binding on the packaging category until superseded.

Background

The agreement indexes the raw material component of packaging prices quarterly, using the European testliner and fluting price index for corrugated articles and the ICIS polyethylene contract price for north-west Europe for flexible articles. The raw material component is fixed at 62% for corrugated and 71% for flexible, with a deadband of plus or minus 2%. During the twelve months to 2026-06-30 the polyethylene index fell by 9.4% while the testliner index rose by 5.1%, producing movements in both directions and exposing three issues that the Council was asked to resolve.

Issue 1 — Asymmetric Application of the Mechanism

Review of the four quarterly adjustments in the period showed that Batavia submitted a calculation promptly on each occasion the indices moved upward, and did not submit a calculation for the Q1 2026 review when the polyethylene index had fallen through the deadband. The reduction was identified by the Vantera category analyst four weeks later and applied retrospectively, recovering €148,000. This is the failure mode described in the direct materials negotiation guide, where the clause is sound but its enforcement is one-sided in practice.

Decision 1: The category analyst will recalculate every indexed article independently from the published indices at each quarterly review, before receiving Batavia's submission, and the two calculations will be reconciled. This becomes a standing control rather than an ad hoc check. Owner: Packaging category analyst. Effective from the Q3 2026 review.

Decision 2: A clarifying amendment will be negotiated confirming that Batavia is obliged to submit a calculation at every quarterly review regardless of the direction of movement, and that a failure to submit does not defer a price reduction, which takes effect from the review date in any event. Owner: Packaging Category Manager, with Legal. Target: 2026-09-30.

Issue 2 — Deadband Carry-Forward Ambiguity

The agreement states that an index movement within the plus or minus 2% deadband does not trigger a price change and is carried forward to the next quarterly review. It does not state whether the carry-forward accumulates across multiple consecutive quarters, or whether it resets. Batavia's interpretation has been that carry-forward resets each quarter, which systematically favours the supplier where several small movements occur in the same direction: three consecutive 1.8% increases produce no price change under a resetting interpretation, but a 5.4% cumulative movement under an accumulating one.

Decision 3: The Council confirms that Vantera's interpretation is that the carry-forward accumulates until the cumulative movement since the last price change exceeds the deadband, at which point the full cumulative movement is applied. This interpretation will be confirmed in the same clarifying amendment as Decision 2. Where Batavia does not accept the interpretation, the matter escalates to the contract dispute process rather than being settled informally at category level. Owner: Packaging Category Manager. Target: 2026-09-30.

Issue 3 — Savings Reporting Treatment

The packaging category reported €148,000 from the retrospective polyethylene adjustment and €310,000 from the general index decline as negotiated savings in the Q1 2026 savings report. Finance challenged this treatment on the basis that a price reduction produced automatically by an agreed mechanism is not a negotiated saving.

Decision 4: The Council upholds the Finance position. From Q3 2026, price movements produced by a contractual indexation mechanism are reported as indexation impact, in a separate line from negotiated savings, in both directions. The €148,000 recovered through enforcement of the mechanism is reported as indexation impact rather than negotiated savings, notwithstanding that identifying it required analyst effort. Reporting mechanical price movements as negotiated performance erodes the credibility of the entire savings figure, which is the reason for the change. Owner: Category Finance business partner. Effective: Q3 2026 report.

Issue 4 — Energy Surcharge Expiry

The energy surcharge introduced by amendment 2 with effect from 2026-04-01, indexed to the Dutch TTF gas benchmark and capped at 4% of the total article price in any 12-month period, expires on 2027-09-30 unless renewed by written agreement.

Decision 5: The Council directs that the surcharge is not renewed by default. A review will be tabled at the Q2 2027 Council meeting assessing whether energy volatility still justifies a separate mechanism or whether the conversion cost element should simply be renegotiated at the next rate review. Owner: Packaging Category Manager. Target: Q2 2027 Council.

Attendance and Approval

Present: Director of Direct Materials (chair), Packaging Category Manager, Category Finance business partner, Head of Packaging Development, Sustainable Procurement representative, Legal Commercial Contracts representative. Decisions were taken unanimously. This memo was approved by the chair on 2026-06-30 and is filed against contract SA-BAT-2025-007 in Ariba Contracts.

title: FAQ — Purchase Orders, Approvals and Starting Work
section_headings: Can a supplier begin work before the purchase order is approved
My approver is on leave and the request is urgent
How is the approval level decided
Can I split a request to keep it under a threshold
The supplier has already invoiced but there is no purchase order
How long will my request take
Can I use my purchasing card instead
I want to add scope to an existing purchase order
Why was my requisition sent back for a statement of work
text:
Can a supplier begin work before the purchase order is approved

No. Suppliers must not begin work, ship goods, or incur cost before an approved purchase order exists. A supplier that starts on the basis of a verbal instruction or an email has no approved commercial cover, and Vantera has no agreed price, scope, or terms. If business continuity genuinely requires work to start first, the emergency purchase route applies: a manager holding the appropriate approval band gives verbal approval, and the requester documents the emergency reason, the estimated spend, the supplier name, and the approving manager's name within 2 business days, with a retrospective purchase order raised within 5 business days.

What counts as an emergency

An emergency is a safety risk, a food safety or quality risk, a regulatory breach, a production stoppage or imminent stoppage, a failure to supply a customer, or a material security incident. A deadline you have known about for weeks, an expiring budget, an approver on holiday, or a contract you let lapse are not emergencies. Using the emergency route for these is a control breach and is reported.

My approver is on leave and the request is urgent

Approvers must set a formal delegation in SAP S/4HANA before going on leave, to someone at the same grade or above. Delegation by email or by sharing credentials is not permitted. If no delegation was set, contact Procurement Operations, who will identify the next appropriate approver in the hierarchy. Do not ask a colleague to approve on the approver's behalf using their account.

How is the approval level decided

By the total committed value of the commitment over its full term, not by the invoice amount and not by the amount falling in this financial year. A three-year service at €20,000 per year is a €60,000 commitment and needs VP Procurement approval with a Finance review, not Category Manager approval. If you are unsure of the value, use a good-faith estimate at the top of the expected range.

Can I split a request to keep it under a threshold

No. Splitting is defined as two or more requisitions for the same supplier and the same scope within a rolling 90-day period whose combined value would have required a higher approval band. It is detected by a monthly report, is treated as a control breach, and is reported to Internal Audit.

The supplier has already invoiced but there is no purchase order

Accounts Payable will not pay an invoice without a valid purchase order, other than for the exempt categories, being utilities, rent, taxes and statutory fees, payroll, insurance premiums, legal settlements, intercompany recharges, and customs duties. The requesting manager must raise a retrospective purchase order using the retrospective flag, stating when the work started and why the order was not raised in advance. If the situation did not meet the emergency definition, it is recorded as an unauthorised commitment and needs approval one band above the level that would normally apply.

How long will my request take

A catalogue purchase converts to a purchase order in about 1 business day if approvals are prompt. Guided buying under an existing framework takes 3 to 5 business days. A three-bid sourcing event takes 4 to 6 weeks from a complete requirement to award. A formal request for proposal takes 8 to 12 weeks to award plus contracting time. Tell Procurement Operations your genuine required date at intake so the realistic route can be chosen.

Do I need three quotes

Three qualified bids are required above €25,000 and up to €250,000 of total committed value. Above €250,000 a formal request for proposal is required. Below €25,000 no formal competition is needed, though you should still be able to show the price is reasonable. If competition is genuinely not possible, a sourcing exception must be approved before the award, not afterwards.

Can I use my purchasing card instead

Only for low-value, low-risk, non-recurring purchases with no catalogue alternative, subject to a €2,500 single-transaction limit and a €10,000 monthly limit. Purchasing cards may not be used for software or subscriptions of any value, services performed on Vantera premises, anything requiring a contract, capital items, contingent labour, or to split a larger purchase into card-sized amounts.

I want to add scope to an existing purchase order

Raise a purchase order amendment before the supplier does the additional work. If the revised total takes the commitment into a higher approval band, the higher band approver must approve, not the original approver.

Why was my requisition sent back for a statement of work

Service requisitions need a statement of work with deliverables, acceptance criteria, and milestone dates. Without them the service cannot be receipted objectively, which is the most common source of disputed invoices in services categories. A description such as consultancy support is not sufficient.

Who do I contact

Procurement Operations for requisition, catalogue, and routing questions. Your Category Manager for supplier selection and negotiation. Accounts Payable for invoice and payment status. The Supplier Risk Office for onboarding and due diligence questions.

title: FAQ — Supplier Onboarding, Invoicing and Payment Status
section_headings: How long does supplier onboarding take
What does the supplier need to provide
Why was the supplier name rejected
Can I enter the supplier's bank details for them
A supplier says they have changed bank account and payment is urgent
When will my supplier be paid
How quickly should a blocked invoice be resolved
Can we pay part of an invoice
Can a supplier be paid early
The supplier is chasing and I cannot see the invoice
text:
How long does supplier onboarding take

Standard onboarding is completed within 10 business days from receipt of a complete submission from the supplier. Expedited onboarding takes 3 business days and requires VP Procurement approval of the business reason. The clock stops whenever the file goes back to the supplier for missing information, which is why most delays are caused by incomplete first submissions rather than by processing time.

What does the supplier need to provide

Certificate of incorporation or equivalent registration, the VAT identification number, a tax residency certificate where withholding tax relief is claimed, bank details entered by the supplier through the Ariba portal, ultimate beneficial ownership details where any shareholder holds 25% or more, acceptance of the Supplier Code of Conduct, and insurance certificates where the category requires them. High-risk suppliers additionally complete an anti-bribery questionnaire and provide registry evidence of beneficial ownership.

Why was the supplier name rejected

The legal name must match the registration document exactly, including the legal form suffix such as S.L., S.L.U., GmbH, Ltd., Inc., B.V., N.V., AG, or Sp. z o.o. Trading names and abbreviations go in the alias field. A mismatch between the legal name and the registration causes failed sanctions screening, payment rejections, and duplicate supplier records, so it is corrected at onboarding rather than later.

Can I enter the supplier's bank details for them

No, under any circumstances, including where the supplier says it cannot access the portal. Bank details are entered by the supplier through its own Ariba portal credentials, and every change is verified by an independent callback to a number taken from the supplier master or the supplier's public registration record, never from the invoice, the email signature, or the request itself. If a supplier is struggling with the portal, raise a ticket with the Supplier Master team rather than working around the control.

A supplier says they have changed bank account and payment is urgent

Treat urgency combined with a bank change as a red flag rather than as a reason to move faster. This is the standard pattern in invoice redirection fraud. The change goes through the portal, requires callback verification and dual approval, and triggers an automatic 24-hour payment hold. Do not process a change from an email, even one that appears to come from a known contact.

When will my supplier be paid

Standard terms are Net 60 from receipt of a valid invoice. Suppliers with turnover below €10,000,000 are paid Net 30. In Spain the statutory maximum of 60 days applies and cannot be extended. The clock starts on receipt of a valid invoice, which means one quoting a valid purchase order number, matching the order and the goods receipt, showing the correct legal entity and VAT registration, and submitted through the Ariba Network.

Why is the invoice blocked

Most blocks are one of five types. A price block means the invoiced price exceeds the purchase order price by more than the 3% tolerance, usually because a price change was agreed commercially but never updated on the order. A quantity block means the invoiced quantity exceeds what was receipted. Goods receipt missing means nobody has confirmed delivery in the system. Purchase order missing or closed means the invoice references no valid open order. A tax block means the VAT treatment or entity details are wrong and a corrected invoice is needed.

What are the automatic tolerances

An invoice posts automatically if the price variance is 3% or less, the quantity variance is 5 units or less, the absolute variance is €50 or less, and the invoice date is no more than 3 calendar days before the goods receipt date. Anything outside these blocks for review.

How quickly should a blocked invoice be resolved

Within 5 business days of assignment. Blocks older than 10 business days escalate to the buyer's line manager, and older than 20 business days to the Category Director. A blocked invoice usually means a supplier has not been paid for goods Vantera has already used, so ageing is treated as a real problem rather than an administrative backlog.

Can we pay part of an invoice

Yes, and we should. Where part of an invoice is disputed, the undisputed portion is paid on the original due date and only the disputed part is withheld. Withholding the whole invoice over a partial dispute is not permitted.

Can a supplier be paid early

Yes, through two routes. A static early payment discount of 2% for payment within 10 days is available on request. The supply chain finance programme lets an approved supplier be paid by a funding bank shortly after invoice approval at a rate based on Vantera's credit rating, while Vantera pays on the original due date. Participation is voluntary and may not be used as negotiating leverage.

The supplier is chasing and I cannot see the invoice

Check first that the invoice was submitted through the Ariba Network rather than emailed to an individual, since invoices sent to a personal mailbox are not in the process at all. Then check whether it was rejected for a missing purchase order number. Accounts Payable can trace an invoice from the supplier's invoice number and the entity it was billed to.

title: Procurement Terminology, Acronyms and Search Reference
text:
Purpose

This reference defines the terms and acronyms used across Vantera procurement documents. It exists because the same concept is frequently named differently by Finance, Legal, and the business, and because search and reporting depend on consistent language.

Process and Transaction Terms

Purchase requisition (PR) is the internal request to buy something, raised in Ariba Buying and subject to approval. Purchase order (PO) is the approved commercial instruction issued to the supplier, and it is the document against which a supplier may begin work. Goods receipt (GR) confirms what was actually delivered and accepted. Service entry sheet is the services equivalent of a goods receipt. Three-way match is the control comparing purchase order, goods receipt, and invoice before payment. Goods received not invoiced (GRNI) is the accrual account holding items received but not yet invoiced. Procure-to-pay (P2P) is the end-to-end process from requisition through to payment. Source-to-contract (S2C) is the upstream process from category strategy through sourcing to a signed contract. Maverick spend is buying outside agreed channels or contracts. Tail spend is the large number of small-value transactions that together represent a minority of spend but a majority of transactions.

Sourcing Terms

Request for information (RFI) gathers market and capability information without pricing commitments. Request for proposal (RFP) is a formal sourcing event with a defined scope, evaluation model, and award process. Request for quotation (RFQ) seeks pricing for a well-defined specification. Best and final offer (BAFO) is a single final pricing round offered to shortlisted bidders on identical terms. Total cost of ownership (TCO) is the full cost of a purchase including acquisition, operation, service, and exit, rather than the purchase price alone. Should-cost is a bottom-up estimate of what an item ought to cost from its input costs. Sole source means only one supplier can meet the requirement. Single source means several could, but Vantera has chosen one. The distinction matters because only sole source is an exception ground under the competitive sourcing policy.

Contract Terms

Master services agreement (MSA) sets the framework terms under which individual services are ordered. Statement of work (SOW) defines the specific scope, deliverables, and price under an MSA. Service level agreement (SLA) defines measurable performance commitments. Key performance indicator (KPI) is a measure reported for management purposes, which may or may not carry a contractual consequence. Service credit is a contractual price reduction payable when an SLA is missed. Limitation of liability caps what a party can be required to pay. Indemnity is a promise to cover defined third-party losses. Termination for convenience is the right to end a contract without cause on notice. Evergreen means a contract that renews indefinitely unless terminated. Order of precedence resolves conflicts between contract documents.

Risk and Compliance Terms

Know your supplier (KYS), also written KYC by analogy with the banking term, is the identity and ownership verification performed at onboarding. Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is the natural person who ultimately owns or controls a supplier. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is the additional verification applied to high-risk suppliers. Anti-bribery and corruption (ABAC) covers the controls preventing improper advantage. Politically exposed person (PEP) is an individual holding a prominent public function. Business email compromise (BEC) is the fraud pattern where a supplier's identity is impersonated to redirect payment. Segregation of duties (SoD) requires that no single person controls a complete transaction. Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) is the United States legislation driving financial control certification requirements.

Data Protection and Security Terms

General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) governs personal data processing in the European Union. Data processing agreement (DPA) is the contract governing a processor's handling of personal data. Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) permit transfers of personal data to third countries. Data Protection Officer (DPO) is the accountable role for data protection. ISO 27001 is the information security management system standard. SOC 2 Type II is an attestation report covering the design and operating effectiveness of controls over a period. Recovery time objective (RTO) is the target time to restore service; recovery point objective (RPO) is the maximum tolerable data loss.

Sustainability Terms

EcoVadis is the third-party sustainability rating used to assess suppliers. Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) sets EU sustainability reporting requirements. Lieferkettensorgfaltspflichtengesetz (LkSG) is the German Supply Chain Due Diligence Act. EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) requires deforestation-free supply chains for listed commodities. Scope 3 emissions are indirect emissions in the value chain, of which category 1 covers purchased goods and services. SMETA is a widely used social audit methodology.

Logistics and Trade Terms

Incoterms are the ICC rules allocating transport cost, risk, and customs responsibility between buyer and seller; the current edition is Incoterms 2020. On-time in-full (OTIF) measures deliveries arriving both on time and complete. Free carrier (FCA), delivered at place (DAP), carriage and insurance paid to (CIP), ex works (EXW), and delivered duty paid (DDP) are individual Incoterms rules. CMR is the convention governing international road carriage. HACCP is the food safety hazard analysis system. Acceptable quality limit (AQL) defines sampling acceptance criteria for incoming inspection.

Search and Reference Note

When searching these documents, note that identifiers such as PO-2026-004417, RFP-EMEA-2026-0141, MSA-ACM-2024-018, and SUP-100482 are exact-match terms, and that legal suffixes, currency amounts such as €50,000, percentages such as 3%, and standards such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II carry meaning that is lost if they are normalised away. Several concepts also appear under more than one label, including purchase order and PO, statement of work and SOW, sole source and single source, and supplier and vendor.
